sentences.zh: [所]建，青龍所躔，參伍以變，錯綜其數，而制術焉。

translations.literal: handle is set, where the Azure Dragon treads, they cross-checked permutations and interwove the numbers, and on that basis they devised the computational methods.
translations.idiomatic: handle is aligned, where the Azure Dragon stands along the sky, matched permutations and interlaced the reckoning until they could set down the algorithms.

sentences.zh: 天之動也，一晝一夜而運過周，星從天而西，日違天而東。

translations.literal: Heaven’s motion: in one day and one night it completes a circuit; the stars move west with Heaven, while the Sun moves east against Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The sky turns once between dusk and dawn; the stars ride westward with it, but the Sun slips eastward against that flow.

sentences.zh: 日之所行與運周，在天成度，在歷成日。

translations.literal: The Sun’s motion and the circuit of the revolution: in the sky they form degrees, in the calendar they form days.
translations.idiomatic: The Sun’s path around the circuit becomes celestial degrees in the sky and counted days on the calendar.

sentences.zh: 居以列宿，終於四七，受以甲乙，終於六旬。

translations.literal: It lodges by the lunar lodges and ends at “four sevens”; it is received in the sexagenary cycle and ends at six decadal pairs.
translations.idiomatic: It is pinned to the twenty-eight lodges (four times seven) and tallied through the sixty-day cycle in ten-day units.

sentences.zh: 日月相推，日舒月速，當其同[所]，謂之合朔。

translations.literal: Sun and Moon push each other: the Sun is slow, the Moon is fast; when they are at the same place, it is called conjunction (new moon).
translations.idiomatic: Sun and Moon chase one another—the Sun lags, the Moon runs ahead—and when they meet in the same longitude we call it new moon.

sentences.zh: 舒先速後，近一遠三，謂之弦。

translations.literal: When [the Sun] is slow first and fast afterward, or near one [side] and far three [parts], it is called “quarter moon” (xian).
translations.idiomatic: When the slow phase leads and the fast follows—near on one limb, farther by three—it is the first or last quarter.

sentences.zh: 相與為衡，分天之中，謂之望。

translations.literal: When they stand opposite each other in balance and divide Heaven at its middle, it is called “full moon” (wang).
translations.idiomatic: When they face each other across the sky and split the heavens down the middle, we have full moon.

sentences.zh: 以速及舒，光盡體伏，謂之晦。

translations.literal: When speed catches up to slowness, light is exhausted and the body hides; it is called “dark” (hui, last day of the month).
translations.idiomatic: When the faster overtakes the slower and the Moon’s light is gone and her disk concealed, that is month’s end, the dark night.

sentences.zh: 晦朔合離，斗建移辰，謂之[月]。

translations.literal: Darkness and conjunction part and join, the Dipper’s handle shifts the hour; this is called the “month.”
translations.idiomatic: New moon and month-end alternate, the Dipper’s handle advances the celestial hour—thus the lunar month is defined.

sentences.zh: [行]，則有冬有夏；

translations.literal: motion, then there is winter and there is summer;
translations.idiomatic: courses, and so we get winter and summer;

sentences.zh: 冬夏之閒，則有春有秋。

translations.literal: between winter and summer, then there is spring and there is autumn.
translations.idiomatic: between those extremes lie spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 是故日行北陸謂之冬，西陸謂之春，南陸謂之夏，東陸謂之秋。

translations.literal: Therefore when the Sun’s path is in the northern quarter it is called winter, in the western quarter spring, in the southern quarter summer, in the eastern quarter autumn.
translations.idiomatic: So the Sun in the northern mansions means winter, in the west spring, in the south summer, in the east autumn.

sentences.zh: 日道發南，去極彌遠，其景彌長，遠長乃極，冬乃至焉。

translations.literal: When the solar path opens toward the south, it goes farther from the pole and the shadow grows longer; when the “far long” reaches its limit, winter arrives.
translations.idiomatic: As the ecliptic tilts south the Sun recedes from the pole, shadows lengthen, and at their greatest length midwinter comes.

sentences.zh: 日道斂北，去極彌近，其景彌短，近短乃極，夏乃至焉。

translations.literal: When the solar path draws in toward the north, it comes nearer the pole and the shadow grows shorter; when the “near short” reaches its limit, summer arrives.
translations.idiomatic: As the path swings north the Sun approaches the pole, shadows shorten, and at their shortest midsummer arrives.

sentences.zh: 二至之中，道齊景正，春秋分焉。

translations.literal: Between the two solstices the path is even and the shadow is true; there spring and autumn equinoxes.
translations.idiomatic: Between the solstices the solar path levels and noon shadows match—those are the spring and autumn equinoxes.

sentences.zh: 日周於天，一寒一暑，四時備成，萬物畢改，攝提遷次，青龍移辰，謂之歲。

translations.literal: The Sun circuits Heaven: one cold and one heat, the four seasons are fully formed, the myriad things all change, Sheti shifts its station, the Azure Dragon moves its hour; this is called a “year.”
translations.idiomatic: One circuit of the Sun brings cold and heat in turn, rounds out the four seasons, renews the myriad things, advances Sheti’s pointer and the Azure Dragon’s station—what we call a year.

sentences.zh: 歲首至也，月首朔也。

translations.literal: The year begins at winter solstice; the month begins at new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The civil year opens at winter solstice; the lunar month opens at new moon.

sentences.zh: 至朔同日謂之章，同在日首謂之蔀，蔀終六旬謂之紀，歲朔又復謂之元。

translations.literal: When solstice and new moon fall on the same day it is called a “chapter” (zhang); when they coincide at the head of the same day it is called a “fold” (bu); when a bu ends at six decadal cycles it is called an “era” (ji); when year and new moon again return together it is called an “origin” (yuan).
translations.idiomatic: Solstice and new moon on one day make a zhang; both starting the same day make a bu; six decadal cycles close a bu and form a ji; when year-start and new moon realign you have a yuan.

sentences.zh: 是故日以實之，月以閏之，時以分之，歲以周之，章以明之，蔀以部之，紀以記之，元以原之。

translations.literal: Therefore the Sun fills it out, the month intercalates it, the seasons divide it, the year cycles it, the zhang clarifies it, the bu organizes it, the ji records it, the yuan traces it to the source.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Sun completes the reckoning, intercalary months adjust it, seasons slice it, the year encloses it, the zhang defines cycles, the bu groups them, the ji logs them, the yuan anchors their beginning.

sentences.zh: 然後雖有變化萬殊，贏朒無方，莫不結繫於此而業正焉。

translations.literal: After that, though changes may be myriad and surplus or deficit follow no fixed rule, nothing fails to tie back to this and find correct alignment here.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the endless variety of calendrical drift, every correction still hooks to these principles and sets the system right.

sentences.zh: 極建其中，道營於外，琁衡追日，以察[發]斂，光道生焉。

translations.literal: The pole is set at the center; the path runs round the outside; the armillary ring tracks the Sun to inspect expansion and contraction, and the bright path [of the ecliptic] is born.
translations.idiomatic: The pole stands at the hub, the ecliptic girdles it, and the armillary instrument tracks the Sun’s advance and retreat—whence the ecliptic itself is derived.

sentences.zh: 孔壺為漏，浮箭為刻，下漏數刻，以考中星，□明生焉。

translations.literal: The perforated clepsydra is the vessel; the floating arrow is the scale; water drips and counts the marks to examine the culminating stars, and clarity [of dusk and dawn] is born.
translations.idiomatic: The pierced pot is the water-clock, the floating rod marks the clepsydra divisions; counting drips against the meridian stars fixes the hours and defines twilight.

sentences.zh: 日有光道，月有九行，九行出入而交生焉。

translations.literal: The Sun has a bright path; the Moon has nine courses; the nine courses go in and out, and intersection is born.
translations.idiomatic: The Sun follows the ecliptic; the Moon has nine paths; where those paths cross, eclipses and nodes appear.

sentences.zh: 朔會望衡，鄰於所交，虧薄生焉。

translations.literal: At new moon they meet; at full moon they balance; they neighbor the place where they cross, and waning and thinning are born.
translations.idiomatic: New moon is their conjunction, full moon their opposition; near the nodes they line up, and partial or total eclipse follows.

sentences.zh: 月有晦朔，星有合見，月有弦望，星有留逆，其歸一也，步術生焉。

translations.literal: The month has last day and new moon; stars have conjunction and appearance; the month has quarters and full moon; stars have station and retrogradation; they return to one principle, and pacing methods are born.
translations.idiomatic: Months have dark and new moons, stars have heliacal rise and visibility, months have quarters and full, stars have stationary points and retrograde loops—all reduce to one method of computation.

sentences.zh: 金、水承陽，先後日下，速則先日，□而後留，留而後逆，逆與日違，違而後速，速與日競，競又先日，□速順逆，晨夕生焉。

translations.literal: Metal and Water receive the Yang; below the Sun, sometimes before and sometimes after; if fast then before the Sun, [if slow] then afterward they stay, stay then retrograde, retrograde then diverge from the Sun, diverge then speed up, speed up then race the Sun, race then again before the Sun; [in] fast, slow, direct, and retrograde, morning and evening are born.
translations.idiomatic: Venus and Mercury ride the sunlight, hugging the Sun inside its orbit: moving fast they outpace it, moving slowly they fall back and halt, halt and then retrograde, slip westward then accelerate again—hence their alternating appearances as morning and evening stars.

sentences.zh: 日、月、五緯各有終原，而七元生焉。

translations.literal: The Sun, Moon, and five luminaries each have their ultimate origins, and the seven “origins” are born.
translations.idiomatic: Sun, Moon, and five planets each have a fundamental period, and from them the seven calendrical “elements” are derived.

sentences.zh: 見伏有日，留行有度，而率數生焉。

translations.literal: Appearance and hiding have days; station and motion have degrees; and mean rates are born.
translations.idiomatic: Heliacal rising and setting take definite days; motion and pause take measured arcs—so mean motions are computed.

sentences.zh: 參差齊之，多少均之，會終生焉。

translations.literal: They are aligned despite inequality, equalized despite difference, and convergence at the end is born.
translations.idiomatic: Unequal motions are averaged, discrepancies reconciled, and the epoch when cycles close is found.

sentences.zh: 引而伸之，觸而長之，探賾索隱，鉤深致遠，無幽辟潛伏，而不以其精者然。

translations.literal: Extend it, stretch it, probe the hidden and search the subtle, hook the deep and reach the far—there is no dark or lurking corner whose essence is not thus laid bare.
translations.idiomatic: Extend the pattern, press every case, sound the hidden depths—nothing in the sky’s recesses escapes this reckoning.

sentences.zh: 故陰陽有分，寒暑有節，天地貞觀，日月貞明。

translations.literal: Therefore Yin and Yang have their divisions, cold and heat have their nodes, Heaven and Earth stand as the constant paradigm, Sun and Moon shine as the constant lights.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yin and Yang part cleanly, cold and heat keep their beats, Heaven and Earth hold a fixed measure, Sun and Moon a steady light.

sentences.zh: 若夫佑術開業，淳耀天光，重黎其上也[1]。

translations.literal: As for those who opened the methods and founded the enterprise, who made Heaven’s glory pure and radiant—Chong and Li were supreme among them[1].
translations.idiomatic: Those who first framed these arts and let celestial splendor shine clear were Chong and Li above all[1].

sentences.zh: 承聖帝之命若昊天，典歷像三辰，以授民事，立閏定時，以成歲功，羲和其隆也[2]。

translations.literal: Receiving the command of the sage emperor as from august Heaven, they regulated the calendar to model the three luminaries and hand seasonal tasks down to the people; they established intercalation and fixed the seasons to complete the year’s work—Xi and He flourished in this[2].
translations.idiomatic: Commissioned like a mandate from Heaven, they aligned the calendar with the three lights to guide the people’s labor, set intercalary rules and nailed the seasons—Xi and He’s glory was in that service[2].

sentences.zh: 取象金火，革命創製，治歷明時，應天順民，湯、武其盛也[3]。

translations.literal: Taking images from metal and fire, they changed the mandate and created new systems, rectified the calendar and clarified the seasons, responding to Heaven and obeying the people—Tang and Wu were greatest in this[3].
translations.idiomatic: They read the omens in the Venus and Mars years, seized the mandate, reformed the system, fixed the calendar to the seasons, matching Heaven and winning the people—Tang of Shang and Wu of Zhou stand highest here[3].

sentences.zh: 及王德之衰也，無道之君亂之於上，頑愚之史失之於下。

translations.literal: When kingly virtue declined, lawless rulers on high threw it into confusion and obstinate clerks below lost it.
translations.idiomatic: When royal virtue failed, reckless sovereigns corrupted the system aloft and dull scribes bungled it below.

sentences.zh: 夏後之時，羲和淫湎，廢時亂日，胤乃征之。

translations.literal: In the time of the Xia heirs, Xi and He indulged in drink, neglected the seasons and threw the days into confusion, and Yin then campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: Under the later Xia, the Xi and He clans drowned in wine, abandoned the calendar and scrambled the days, until Yin’s punitive expedition was launched.

sentences.zh: 紂作淫虐，喪其甲子，武王誅之。

translations.literal: Zhou practiced debauchery and cruelty and lost track of his jiazi day-count; King Wu executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The last king of Shang gave himself to cruelty and lost even his day-count; King Wu overthrew him.

sentences.zh: 夫能貞而明之者，其興也勃焉；

translations.literal: Those who can keep it correct and bright—their rise is vigorous;
translations.idiomatic: States that honor true calendrical order rise with sudden force;

sentences.zh: 回而敗之者，其亡也忽焉。

translations.literal: those who turn away and ruin it—their fall is swift.
translations.idiomatic: those that twist or break it collapse overnight.

sentences.zh: 巍巍乎若道天地之綱紀，帝王之壯事，是以聖人寶焉，君子勤之。

translations.literal: How lofty! As if it were the warp and woof of Heaven and Earth, the great enterprise of emperors and kings—therefore the sages treasure it and gentlemen labor at it.
translations.idiomatic: So august is this art—the very fabric of cosmos and the crown work of kings—that sages cherish it and gentlemen toil at it without rest.

sentences.zh: 夫歷有聖人之德六焉：以本氣者尚其體，以綜數者尚其文，以考類者尚其象，以作事者尚其時，以占往者尚其源，以知來者尚其流。

translations.literal: The calendar has six kinds of sage virtue: those who take original qi esteem the substance; those who weave numbers esteem the pattern; those who examine analogies esteem the images; those who undertake affairs esteem the timeliness; those who investigate the past esteem the source; those who know the future esteem the downstream flow.
translations.idiomatic: Calendrical science wears six virtues of the sage: root it in vital qi for its body, braid the numbers for its pattern, compare types for its imagery, time undertakings by it, trace antiquity to its source, and read the future in its drift.

sentences.zh: 大業載之，吉凶生焉，是以君子將有興焉，咨焉而以從事，受命而莫之違也。

translations.literal: The great enterprise rides upon it; good and ill are born from it—therefore when a gentleman is about to undertake something, he consults it and follows it; having received the mandate, he does not disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Great undertakings rest on it; fortune and misfortune flow from it—so the gentleman consults these reckonings before acting and, once charged, does not defy Heaven’s measure.

sentences.zh: 若夫用天因地，揆時施教，頒諸明堂，以為民極者，莫大乎月令。

translations.literal: As for using Heaven and grounding it in Earth, measuring the seasons to spread instruction, promulgating it in the Bright Hall, and making a norm for the people—nothing is greater than the “Monthly Ordinances.”
translations.idiomatic: Nothing matches the Monthly Ordinances for aligning Heaven and Earth, timing the edicts, and publishing them in the Bright Hall as the people’s standard.

sentences.zh: 帝王之大司備矣，天下之能事畢矣。

translations.literal: The great offices of emperors and kings are complete; the world’s possible tasks are finished.
translations.idiomatic: With that, the sovereign’s great calendar is whole and every task under Heaven is covered.

sentences.zh: 過此而往，腢忌苟禁，君子未之或知也。

translations.literal: Beyond this, petty taboos and careless prohibitions—the gentleman has never thought it worth knowing.
translations.idiomatic: Past that lie minor divinatory taboos and arbitrary bans—topics a serious scholar does not bother with.

sentences.zh: 斗之二十一度，去極至遠也，日在焉而冬至，腢物於是乎生。

translations.literal: At twenty-one degrees of the Dipper’s [path] the distance to the pole is greatest; the Sun is there at winter solstice, and the myriad things are thereby generated.
translations.idiomatic: Where the Dipper’s circle stands twenty-one degrees from the pole—winter solstice—the Sun lies farthest south and the myriad things begin their yearly renewal.

sentences.zh: 故律首黃鐘，歷始冬至，月先建子，時平夜半。

translations.literal: Therefore the pitchpipes begin with Yellow Bell; the calendar begins at winter solstice; the month takes the jian-zi month first; the hour balances at midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the pitch sequence starts with Yellow Bell, the civil year at winter solstice, the month series with jianzi, the day-count from midnight.

sentences.zh: 當漢高皇帝受命四十有五歲，陽在上章，陰在執徐，冬十有一月甲子夜半朔旦冬至，日月閏積之數皆自此始，立元正朔，謂之漢歷。

translations.literal: When forty-five years had passed from the Han Emperor Gaozu’s receiving the mandate, the Yang [stem] was shangzhang, the Yin [branch] was zhixu, in the eleventh month of winter, jiazi day, midnight, new moon and winter solstice coincided; the accumulated numbers for intercalary months and the five planets all began from this point; they established the origin and corrected the first month—this is called the Han calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-five years after Gaozu founded the Han, on a jiazi midnight in the eleventh winter month—new moon and solstice together—the grand conjunction of intercalation and planetary epochs was fixed; they set the epoch and standard month, and that is the Han calendar.

sentences.zh: 又上兩元，而月食五星之元，並發端焉。

translations.literal: Further, going up two earlier yuans, the origins of lunar eclipses and the five planets also begin from there.
translations.idiomatic: Push two higher epochs back from that point and the eclipse cycle and five-planet epochs all start there too.

sentences.zh: 歷數之生也，乃立儀、表，以校日景。

translations.literal: When calendrical numbers arise, one sets up a gnomon and table to measure the solar shadow.
translations.idiomatic: To derive the basic numbers you erect a gnomon and shadow-table and read the noon shadow.

sentences.zh: 景長則日遠，天度之端也。

translations.literal: When the shadow is long, the Sun is far away; that is the end-point of celestial degrees.
translations.idiomatic: A longer shadow means a more distant Sun—that marks the limit of the solar degree.

sentences.zh: 日發其端，周而為歲，然其景不復，四周千四百六十一日，而景復初，是則日行之終。

translations.literal: The Sun departs from that end-point and circuits to make a year, yet its shadow does not return the same; after four circuits—1,461 days—the shadow returns to the beginning; this is the end of the Sun’s motion.
translations.idiomatic: The Sun leaves that point and tours the sky for a year, but the shadow does not repeat until four such cycles—1,461 days—when the gnomon reading matches the start: one complete solar period.

sentences.zh: 以周除日，得三百六十五四分度之一，為歲之日數。

translations.literal: Dividing days by circuits, one obtains 365 and 1/4 days as the number of days in a year.
translations.idiomatic: Divide those days by four circuits and you get 365¼ days for the tropical year.

sentences.zh: 日日行一度，亦為天度。

translations.literal: The Sun travels one degree each day; this also is a celestial degree.
translations.idiomatic: The Sun moves one degree a day—that is both a solar day and a sky degree.

sentences.zh: 察日月俱發度端[4]，日行十九周，月行二百五十四周，復會於端，是則月行之終也。

translations.literal: Observing that Sun and Moon both depart from the degree-origin[4], the Sun makes nineteen circuits while the Moon makes 254 circuits, and they meet again at the origin—this is the end of the Moon’s motion.
translations.idiomatic: From a common starting longitude the Sun completes nineteen revolutions while the Moon makes 254 and they conjoin again—closing the Moon’s cycle.

sentences.zh: 以日周除月周，得一歲周天之數。

translations.literal: Dividing the Moon’s circuits by the Sun’s circuits, one obtains the number of lunar revolutions in one year.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the Moon’s revolutions by the Sun’s and you have how many sidereal months fit a year.

sentences.zh: 以日一週減之，余十二十九分之七，則月行過周及日行之數也，為一歲之月。

translations.literal: Subtract one solar circuit from it; the remainder is 10 and 7/29; that is the excess by which the Moon’s circuit surpasses the Sun’s circuit in one year, and it is the number of months in one year.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract one solar revolution and the remainder is 10 7/29—the Moon’s yearly advance over the Sun—which yields the synodic months in a year.

sentences.zh: 以除一歲日，為一月之數。

translations.literal: Dividing it into the days of one year gives the number for one month.
translations.idiomatic: Divide that into the days of a year to get the mean length of a month.

sentences.zh: 月之餘分積滿其法，得一月，月成則其歲[大]。

translations.literal: When the fractional remainders of the month fill their divisor, they make one month; when the month is complete, then the year is [great].
translations.idiomatic: When leftover parts of a month add up to a full divisor you gain a month; when the months line up, the year is reckoned “long.”

sentences.zh: 四時推移，故置十二中以定月位。

translations.literal: The four seasons shift; therefore one sets twelve mid-month qi to fix the month’s place.
translations.idiomatic: As the seasons turn, twelve “central” qi are inserted to anchor each lunar month.

sentences.zh: 有朔而無中者為閏月。

translations.literal: A month that has new moon but no mid-qi is an intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: If a month contains a new moon but never receives its mid-qi, that month is intercalated.

sentences.zh: [曰]節，與中為二十四氣。

translations.literal: is called a “seasonal node” (jie); together with the mid-qi they make the twenty-four qi.
translations.idiomatic: qi segment is a jie; paired with the zhong qi you have all twenty-four solar terms.

sentences.zh: 以除一歲日，為一氣之日數也。

translations.literal: Dividing this into the days of one year gives the number of days for one qi.
translations.idiomatic: Spread the year’s days across them and you get the mean length of one qi.

sentences.zh: 其分積而成日為沒，並歲氣之分，如法為一歲沒。

translations.literal: Their fractions accumulating into days form the “submergence” (mo); combining the year’s qi fractions according to the rule gives one year’s mo.
translations.idiomatic: Leftover fractions pile into “submergence” days; summed against the rule they give the yearly mo total.

translations.idiomatic: Multiply solstice minor remainder by fifteen, subtract from the common divisor; each mo divisor in the result is the post–new-year mo.

sentences.zh: [蔀月]乘之，滿大周除去之，其余滿蔀月得一，名為積度，不盡為余分。

translations.literal: [bu months] multiply them; remove full great cycles; with the remainder, when it fills bu months, that is one—call it accumulated degrees; what is not exhausted is fractional parts.
translations.idiomatic: …× bu months, drop whole great cycles, fold remainders into accumulated degrees and fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 積度加斗二十一度，加二百三十五分，以宿次除之，不滿宿，則日月合朔所在星度也。

translations.literal: To accumulated degrees add 21 degrees of the Dipper plus 235 parts; remove by lunar-lodge steps; what does not fill a lodge is the star degree where Sun and Moon conjoin at new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Add 21°35′ of Dipper measure, step through lodges; the residue is conjunction’s sidereal place.

sentences.zh: 求後合朔，加度二十九，加分四百九十九，分滿蔀月得一度，經斗除二百三十五分。

translations.literal: To seek the next conjunction: add 29 degrees and 499 parts to the fraction; when the fraction fills bu months, obtain one degree; passing through the Dipper, remove 235 parts.
translations.idiomatic: Next conjunction: +29° +499 parts, carry a degree per bu month, subtract 235 parts when crossing the Dipper field.

sentences.zh: 一術，以閏余乘周天，以減大周余，滿蔀月得一，合以斗二十一度四分一，則天正合朔日月所在度。

translations.literal: One method: multiply the intercalary remainder by the celestial circumference, subtract from the great-cycle remainder; when the remainder fills bu months, add together with 21 degrees and one-quarter of a degree of the Dipper—then that is the degrees where Sun and Moon conjoin at celestial-standard new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Shortcut: great-cycle residue minus intercalary remainder × celestial circumference, folded by bu months, plus 21¼° Dipper—gives conjunction longitude for civil new moon.

sentences.zh: 推日所在度，置入蔀積日之數，以蔀法乘之，滿蔀日除去之，其餘滿蔀法得一，為積度，不盡為余分。

translations.literal: To push the Sun’s degree: set the count of accumulated days within the bu, multiply by the bu rule; remove bu days; with the remainder, when it fills the bu rule, that is one—call it accumulated degrees; what is not exhausted is fractional parts.
translations.idiomatic: Solar longitude: accumulated bu days × bu rule, modulo bu days and bu rule into degrees and fractions.

sentences.zh: 積度加斗二十一度，加十九分，以宿次除去之，則夜半日所在宿度也。

translations.literal: To accumulated degrees add 21 degrees of the Dipper plus 19 parts; remove by lodge steps as above—then that is the lodge and degree where the Sun is at midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Add 21°19′ Dipper, reduce by lodges—the midnight Sun position.

sentences.zh: 求次日，加一度。

translations.literal: To seek the next day: add one degree.
translations.idiomatic: For the next night: add 1°.

sentences.zh: 求次月，大加三十度，小加二十九度，經斗除十[九]分。

translations.literal: To seek the next month: for a long month add 30 degrees, for a short month 29 degrees; passing through the Dipper, remove ten[nine] parts.
translations.idiomatic: Next month: +30° if long, +29° if short; subtract 19 parts when threading the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 一術，以朔小余減合[朔]度分，即日夜半所在。

translations.literal: One method: subtract conjunction degree-parts from the new-moon minor remainder—then that is where [the Sun] is at midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Alternate: new-moon minor remainder minus conjunction fraction gives midnight solar longitude.

sentences.zh: 推月所在度，置入蔀積日之數，以月周乘之，滿蔀日除去之，其餘滿蔀法得一，為積度，不盡為余分。

translations.literal: To push the Moon’s degree: set the count of accumulated days within the bu, multiply by the lunar cycle; remove bu days; with the remainder, when it fills the bu rule, that is one—call it accumulated degrees; what is not exhausted is fractional parts.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar longitude: bu accumulated days × lunar cycle, same reduction into degrees and parts.

sentences.zh: 積度加斗二十一十[九]分，除如上法，則所求之日夜半月所在宿度也。

translations.literal: To accumulated degrees add 21 degrees and 19 fen of the Dipper; remove as in the rule above—then that is the lodge and degree where the Moon is at midnight on the night sought.
translations.idiomatic: Add the Dipper offset of 21°19′, then lodge-reduce as before—that is midnight lunar longitude for the night in question.

sentences.zh: 求次日，加十三度二十八分。

translations.literal: To seek the next day: add 13 degrees and 28 parts.
translations.idiomatic: Next day: +13°28′.

sentences.zh: 求次月，大加三十五度六十一分，月小二十二度三十三分，分滿法得一度，經斗除十九分。

translations.literal: To seek the next month: for a long month add 35 degrees and 61 parts; for a short month 22 degrees and 33 parts; when parts fill the divisor, obtain one degree; passing through the Dipper, remove 19 parts.
translations.idiomatic: Next month: long +35°61′, short +22°33′, carry degrees, subtract 19 parts at the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 一術，以蔀法除朔小余，所得以減日半度也。

translations.literal: One method: divide the new-moon minor remainder by the bu rule; what you obtain, subtract from half a day.
translations.idiomatic: Shortcut: new-moon minor remainder ÷ bu rule, subtracted from half a day.

sentences.zh: 余以減分，即月夜半所在度也。

translations.literal: Use the remainder to subtract from the parts—then that is the Moon’s midnight degree.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract that from the fractional column to get midnight lunar longitude.

sentences.zh: 推日明所入度分術曰：置其月節氣夜漏之數，以蔀法乘之，二百除之，得一分，即夜半到明所行分也。

translations.literal: The method for the Sun’s brightness-entry degree-parts says: set that month’s solar-term night-drip count, multiply by the bu rule, divide by two hundred; what you obtain as one part is the motion from midnight to dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Dawn Sun: take the term’s night drip × bu rule ÷ 200 for degrees moved before sunrise.

sentences.zh: 以增夜半日所在度分，為明所在度分也。

translations.literal: Add that to the midnight Sun degree-parts—then that is the degree-parts where brightness is.
translations.idiomatic: Add to midnight solar longitude for dawn position.

sentences.zh: 求□月所入度：以明積分減月周，其餘滿蔀法得一度，加夜半，則□月所在度也。

translations.literal: To seek □ month’s entry degree: subtract bright accumulated parts from the lunar cycle; with the remainder, when it fills the bu divisor, that is one degree; add to midnight—then □ month’s degree where it stands.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month’s longitude: subtract dawn’s fractional advance from one lunar cycle; each full bu divisor adds one degree to midnight’s position—that gives the Moon’s place for that month.

sentences.zh: 推弦、望日所入星度術曰：置合朔度分之數，加七度三百五十九分四分

sentences.zh: 三，[以]宿次除之，即得上弦日所入宿度分也。

translations.literal: three, [and] remove by lunar-lodge steps—then you obtain the lodge and degree where the first-quarter day enters.
translations.idiomatic: …then lodge-reduce to get the first quarter’s sidereal position.

sentences.zh: 求望、下弦，加除如前法，小分[滿]四從大分，[大分]滿蔀月從度。

translations.literal: To seek full moon and last quarter, add and remove as in the previous rule; when small parts fill four, carry to large parts; when large parts fill bu months, carry to degrees.
translations.idiomatic: For full and last quarters, repeat the same addition and reduction; carry small parts into large parts by fours, and large parts into degrees when they fill a bu month.

sentences.zh: 推弦、望月所入星度術曰：置月合朔度分之數，加度九十八，加分六百五十三半，以宿次除之，即上弦月所入宿度分也。

translations.literal: The method for the star degrees where the Moon at quarter and full moon falls says: set the Moon’s conjunction degree-and-parts count, add ninety-eight degrees and six hundred fifty-three and a half parts, remove by lunar-lodge steps—then you obtain the lodge and degree where the first-quarter Moon enters.
translations.idiomatic: For the Moon at quarters: from conjunction longitude add 98°653½′, then lodge-reduce—that is first-quarter lunar longitude.

sentences.zh: 求望、下弦，加除如前分，滿蔀月從度。

translations.literal: To seek full moon and last quarter, add and remove as in the previous parts; when it fills bu months, carry to degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Step to full and last quarters the same way, carrying a full bu month of parts into whole degrees.

sentences.zh: 推月食術曰：置入蔀會年數，減一，以食數乘之，滿歲數得一，名曰積食，不滿為食余。

translations.literal: The method for pushing lunar eclipses says: set the count of years entered in the bu hui, subtract one, multiply by the eclipse number; when it fills the year-number, that is one—call it accumulated eclipses; what does not fill is eclipse remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipse reckoning: (bu-hui years − 1) × eclipse number, folded by the year divisor into accumulated eclipses and remainder.

sentences.zh: 以月數乘積[食]，滿食法得一，名為積月，不滿為月餘分。

translations.literal: Multiply accumulated [eclipse] by the month number; when it fills the eclipse divisor, that is one—call it accumulated months; what does not fill is fractional month parts.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply accumulated eclipses by the month constant; reduce by the eclipse divisor into whole months and leftover parts.

sentences.zh: 積月以章月除去之，其餘為入章月數。

translations.literal: Remove zhang months from accumulated months; the remainder is the count of months entered into the zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Strip whole zhang-month periods from accumulated months; what remains counts months within the current zhang.

sentences.zh: 當先除入章閏，乃以十二除去之，不滿者命以十一月，筭盡之外，則前年十一月前食月也。

translations.literal: One must first remove intercalation entered into the zhang, then remove by twelve; what does not fill, name starting from the eleventh month; beyond where the count is exhausted—that is the month before last year’s eleventh month in which the eclipse falls.
translations.idiomatic: First clear the zhang’s intercalary offset, then reduce by twelve; name from month XI; the exhausted count lands on the eclipse month before the prior year’s eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 求入章閏者，置入章月，以章閏乘之，滿章月得一，則入章閏數也。

translations.literal: To seek intercalation entered into the zhang: set months entered into the zhang, multiply by zhang intercalation; when it fills zhang months, that is one—then that is the count of intercalation entered into the zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalation within the zhang: months-in-zhang × zhang intercalation, divided by zhang months.

sentences.zh: 余分滿二百二十四以上至二百三十一，為食在閏月。

translations.literal: If the remainder parts are 224 or more up to 231, the eclipse falls in an intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: Remainders from 224 through 231 put the eclipse in a leap month.

sentences.zh: 閏或進退，以朔日定之。

translations.literal: The intercalary month may advance or retreat one; fix it by the new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: Adjust the leap month ±1 as needed to match the new-moon reckoning.

translations.literal: [months] twenty parts; when it fills the divisor, that is one month’s count; name it according to the rule; when the parts are exhausted, the eclipse is above the count.
translations.idiomatic: …hundred twenty fractional parts; each full divisor adds a month; name as usual; zero remainder means the eclipse sits on the named day.

sentences.zh: 推月食朔日術曰：置食積月之數，以二十九乘之，為積日。

translations.literal: The method for pushing the lunar-eclipse new-moon day says: set the count of accumulated eclipse months, multiply it by twenty-nine—this is accumulated days.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipse new moon: accumulated eclipse months × 29 gives accumulated days.

sentences.zh: 又以四百九十[九]乘積月，滿蔀月得一，以並積日，以六十除之，其餘以所會蔀名命之，筭盡之外，則前年天正前食月朔日也。

translations.literal: Also multiply accumulated months by four hundred ninety-nine; when it fills bu months, that is one; add it to accumulated days; remove sixties; name the remainder with the bu title you are in; beyond where the count is exhausted—that is last year’s celestial-standard month before the eclipse’s new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: Add 499 × accumulated months with bu-month carry into days, reduce modulo sixty, read against the bu name—the exhausted count is the new moon before the eclipse month in the prior civil year.

sentences.zh: 求食日，加大余十四，小余七百一十九半，小余滿蔀月為大余，大余命如前，則食日也。

translations.literal: To seek the eclipse day: add fourteen to the major remainder and seven hundred nineteen and a half to the minor remainder; when the minor remainder fills bu months, it becomes major remainder; name the major remainder as before—then that is the eclipse day.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipse day: +14 major, +719½ minor; carry bu months into major; name stems and branches—that is eclipse day.

sentences.zh: 求後食朔及日，皆加大余二十七，小余六百一十五。

translations.literal: To seek the next eclipse’s new moon and day, in each case add twenty-seven to the major remainder and six hundred fifteen to the minor remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Each following eclipse: +27 major, +615 minor (with standard carries).

sentences.zh: 其月餘分不滿二十者，又加大余二十九，小余四百九十九。

translations.literal: If the month’s remainder parts do not reach twenty, again add twenty-nine to the major remainder and four hundred ninety-nine to the minor remainder.
translations.idiomatic: If month remainder < 20, add another +29 major and +499 minor.

sentences.zh: 其食小餘者，當以漏刻課之，夜漏未盡，以筭上為日。

translations.literal: If there is fractional eclipse remainder, one should measure it with clepsydra marks; if the night drip is not yet exhausted, take what is above the count as the day.
translations.idiomatic: Fractional eclipse times need clepsydra conversion; if night drip has not run out, the event still belongs to the previous civil day.

sentences.zh: 一術，以歲數去上元，余以為積月，以百一十二乘之，滿月數去之，余滿食法得一，則天正後食。

translations.literal: One method: remove the year-number from the high yuan; take the remainder as accumulated months; multiply by one hundred twelve; remove full month-numbers; when the remainder fills the eclipse divisor, that is one—then it is the eclipse after celestial-standard [new year].
translations.idiomatic: Shortcut: high-yuan residue → ×112 → reduce by month number → fold by eclipse divisor for the first post–new-year eclipse.

sentences.zh: 推諸加時，以十二乘小余，先減如法之半，得一時，其餘乃以法除之，所得筭之數從夜半子起，筭盡之外，則所加時也。

translations.literal: To push all added double-hours: multiply the minor remainder by twelve; first subtract half of the divisor according to the rule; what you obtain is one double-hour; the remainder then divide by the divisor; take the quotient and count the number from midnight zi; beyond where the count is exhausted—that is the added double-hour.
translations.idiomatic: Convert fractional day to the twelve double-hours: 12 × minor remainder, adjust by half the rule, divide for the hour count from midnight zi.

sentences.zh: 推諸上水漏刻：以百乘其小余，滿其法得一刻；

translations.idiomatic: Clepsydra marks after midnight: minor remainder × 100 ÷ rule = whole ke.

sentences.zh: 推五星術，置上元以來，盡所求年，以周率乘之，滿日率得一，名為積合；

translations.literal: The method for pushing the five planets: from the high yuan down to the year sought, multiply by the circumferential rate; when it fills the day rate, that is one—call it accumulated conjunction;
translations.idiomatic: For planetary conjunctions: years since high yuan × circumferential rate ÷ day rate gives accumulated conjunctions;

sentences.zh: 不盡名[為]合余。

translations.literal: what is not exhausted is named [as] conjunction remainder.
translations.idiomatic: the undivided part is conjunction remainder.

sentences.zh: [合]余以周率除之，不得焉退歲；

translations.literal: [Conjunction] remainder divided by the circumferential rate: if it does not go, retreat one year;
translations.idiomatic: Divide conjunction remainder by the circumferential rate; if it fails to divide, step back one year;

sentences.zh: 無所得，星合其年，得一合前年，二合前二年。

translations.literal: if there is no quotient, the star conjoins in that year; if one, it conjoined the previous year; if two, two years before.
translations.idiomatic: no quotient means conjunction this year, one means last year, two means two years prior.

sentences.zh: 金、水積合奇為晨，偶為夕。

translations.literal: For metal and water, if accumulated conjunctions is odd it is morning, if even it is evening.
translations.idiomatic: Venus and Mercury: odd accumulated conjunction counts as a morning apparition, even as an evening one.

sentences.zh: 其不滿周率者反減之，余為度分。

translations.literal: What does not fill the circumferential rate, reverse-subtract it; the remainder is degrees and parts.
translations.idiomatic: Take the shortfall below one circumferential rate, subtract it from the rate; the residue is ecliptic longitude in degrees.

sentences.zh: 推星合月，以合積月乘積合為小積，又以月餘乘積合，滿其月法得一，從小積[為積月，不盡]為月餘。

translations.literal: To push the star’s conjunction month: multiply accumulated conjunction by conjunction accumulated months to make small accumulation; also multiply accumulated conjunction by month remainder; when it fills its month method, that is one—add to small accumulation [to make accumulated months; what is not exhausted] is month remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Conjunction month: conjunction count × synodic months plus cross-terms with month remainder, reduced by the month divisor into accumulated months and fractional remainder.

sentences.zh: 積月滿紀月去之，余為入紀月。

translations.literal: Remove full ji months from accumulated months; the remainder is months entered into the ji.
translations.idiomatic: Modulo ji months gives position within the ji cycle.

sentences.zh: 每以章閏乘之，滿章月得一為閏；

translations.literal: In each case multiply by zhang intercalation; when it fills zhang months, that is one—intercalation;
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by zhang intercalation; each full zhang month adds an intercalary slot;

sentences.zh: 不盡為閏余。

translations.literal: what is not exhausted is intercalary remainder.
translations.idiomatic: the leftover is intercalary fractional remainder.

sentences.zh: 以閏減入紀月，其餘以十二去之，余為入歲月數，從天正十一月起，筭外，星合所在之月也。

translations.literal: Subtract intercalation from months entered into the ji; remove twelve from the remainder; the remainder is the count of months entered into the year, counting from celestial-standard eleventh month; beyond the count—that is the month in which the star conjoins.
translations.idiomatic: Strip leap from ji months, reduce by twelve, count from month XI—where the tally ends is conjunction’s civil month.

sentences.zh: 其閏[余]滿二百二十四以上至二百三十一星合閏月。

translations.literal: If intercalary [remainder] is 224 up to 231, the star conjoins in an intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary remainders 224–231 place conjunction in a leap month.

sentences.zh: 閏或進退，以朔制之。

translations.literal: The intercalary month may advance or retreat one; control it by the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Adjust the leap month ±1 to match new-moon placement.

translations.idiomatic: New moon day: multiply bu days by

translations.literal: (it)

sentences.zh: 入紀月，滿蔀月得一為積日，不盡為小余。

translations.literal: months entered into the ji; when it fills bu months, that is one—accumulated days; what is not exhausted is minor remainder.
translations.idiomatic: …months-in-ji; each bu month folds into accumulated days with minor remainder.

sentences.zh: 積日滿六十去之，余為大余，命以甲子，筭外，星合月朔日。

translations.literal: Remove sixties from accumulated days; the remainder is major remainder; name it with jiazi; beyond the count—that is the new-moon day of the star’s conjunction month.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce days modulo sixty, name with sexagenary cycle—the exhausted count is conjunction new moon.

sentences.zh: 推入月日，以蔀日乘月餘，以其月法乘朔小余，從之，以四千四百六十五約之，所得

translations.literal: To push days entered into the month: multiply bu days by month remainder, multiply month method by new-moon minor remainder, add them together, reduce by four thousand four hundred sixty-five; what you obtain
translations.idiomatic: Days into synodic month: (bu days × month remainder + month method × new-moon minor) ÷ 4465 yields

translations.literal: (obtain)

sentences.zh: 滿日度法得一，為入月日，不盡為日餘。

translations.literal: when it fills the day-degree method, that is one—days entered into the month; what is not exhausted is day remainder.
translations.idiomatic: …quotient folded by the degree-day divisor into whole days and day remainder.

sentences.zh: 以朔命入月日，筭外，星合日也。

translations.literal: Name by the new moon the days entered into the month; beyond the count—that is the star’s conjunction day.
translations.idiomatic: Read against new moon to name the day-within-month of conjunction.

sentences.zh: 推合度，以周天乘度分，滿日度法得一為積度，不盡為度余。

translations.literal: To push conjunction degrees: multiply the full circle of Heaven by degree parts; when it fills the day-degree method, that is one—accumulated degrees; what is not exhausted is degree remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Conjunction longitude: celestial circumference × fractional parts ÷ day-degree method.

sentences.zh: 以斗二十一四分之一命度，筭外，星合所在度也。

translations.literal: Name degrees from twenty-one and one-quarter degrees of the Dipper; beyond the count—that is the degree where the star conjoins.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce from 21¼° in the Dipper field to get conjunction ecliptic longitude.

sentences.zh: 一術，加退歲一，以減上元，滿八十除去之，余以沒數乘之，滿日法得一，為大余，不盡為小余。

translations.literal: One method: add one to the retreat year, subtract from the high yuan; remove full eighties; multiply the remainder by the mo number; when it fills the day rule, that is one—major remainder; what is not exhausted is minor remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Alternate: (high yuan − retreat year − 1) mod 80 × mo number, reduced to major and minor remainders.

sentences.zh: 以甲子命大余，則星合歲天正冬至日也。

translations.literal: Name the major remainder with jiazi—then that is the winter-solstice day of the star’s conjunction year in celestial-standard reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Sexagenary major remainder names conjunction-year winter solstice in the civil calendar.

sentences.zh: 以周率[乘]小余，並度余，余滿日度法從度，即

translations.literal: Multiply the circumferential rate by [the] minor remainder and add degree remainder; when the remainder fills the day-degree method, carry to degrees—then
translations.idiomatic: Circumferential rate × minor remainder + degree remainder, carried by the degree divisor—then

translations.literal: (correct)
translations.idiomatic: The gloss reads ‘correct’ for the alignment.

sentences.zh: [至]後星合日數也，命以冬至。

translations.literal: [to] after the star’s conjunction day-count; name from winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: …you have days after solstice to conjunction; count from winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 求後合月，加合積月於入歲月，加月餘於月餘，滿其月法得一，從入歲月。

translations.literal: To seek the next conjunction month: add conjunction accumulated months to months entered into the year; add month remainder to month remainder; when it fills its month method, that is one—carry to months entered into the year.
translations.idiomatic: Step conjunction month: add synodic months and remainders with carries into the civil year count.

sentences.zh: 入歲月滿十二去之，有閏計焉，余命如前，筭外，後合月也。

translations.literal: Remove twelve from months entered into the year; if there is intercalation, account for it; name the remainder as before; beyond the count—that is the next conjunction month.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce by twelve with leap adjustment; name as before for the following conjunction month.

translations.literal: [Metal, water:] add morning to get evening, add evening to get morning.
translations.idiomatic: For Venus and Mercury, toggling morning and evening apparitions each cycle.

sentences.zh: 求朔日，以大小余加今所得，其月餘得一月者，又[加大]余二十九，[小余四百九十九，]小飾滿蔀月得一，

translations.literal: To seek the new-moon day: add major and minor remainders to what you now have; if the month remainder attains one month, again [add major] remainder twenty-nine, [minor remainder four hundred ninety-nine;] when minor remainder fills bu months, that is one,

sentences.zh: [加]大余，大余命如前。

translations.idiomatic: …then add to major remainder and name stems and branches as before.

sentences.zh: 求入月日，以入月日[日]余加今所得，余滿日度法得一，從日。

translations.literal: To seek days entered into the month: add day entered-into-month [and] day remainder to what you now have; when remainder fills the day-degree method, that is one—carry to days.
translations.idiomatic: Update days-in-month by adding day parts with carry through the degree-day divisor.

translations.literal: fill its void fraction, vacuously add one day.
translations.idiomatic: fails to reach its empty fraction, insert an extra day in the count.

sentences.zh: 日滿月先去二十九，其後合月朔小余不滿四百九十九，又減一日，其餘命如前。

translations.literal: When days fill the month, first remove twenty-nine; if thereafter the conjunction month’s new-moon minor remainder does not fill four hundred ninety-nine, again subtract one day; name the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: On month rollover subtract 29 first; if new moon minor <499, subtract another day; then name as usual.

sentences.zh: 求合度，以積度度余加今所得，余滿日度法得一從度，命如前，經斗除如周率矣。

translations.literal: To seek conjunction degrees: add accumulated degrees and degree remainder to what you now have; when remainder fills the day-degree method, that is one—carry to degrees; name as before; passing through the Dipper, remove as with the circumferential rate.
translations.idiomatic: Advance longitude by accumulated degrees and parts, carry through the divisor, Dipper-subtract like the circumferential step.

translations.literal: [three] hundred twenty parts and a half; it moves two degrees and thirteen thousand eight hundred eleven parts; slightly more than thirteen degrees behind the Sun, and appears in the east.
translations.idiomatic: …723½ fractional parts; motion 2°13,811′; about 13° east of the Sun at heliacal rise.

sentences.zh: 見順，日行五十八分度之十一，五十八日行十一度，微□，日行九分，五十八日行九度。

translations.literal: Visible direct: it travels eleven parts in fifty-eighths of a degree per day; in fifty-eight days it travels eleven degrees; slightly □, nine parts per day; in fifty-eight days it travels nine degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Direct motion: 11/58° per day for 58 days (11°), then a slower 9/58° per day for another 58 days (9°).

translations.idiomatic: Early Waking of Insects: leg ulcers and shin edema.

sentences.zh: 春分，晷長七尺二寸四分。

translations.literal: Spring Equinox: shadow length seven chi two cun four fen.
translations.idiomatic: Spring Equinox: noon shadow 7 chi 2 cun 4 fen.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，先旱後水，歲惡，米不成，多病耳癢。

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, first drought then water; the year is bad; rice does not ripen; many itchy ears.
translations.idiomatic: Late equinox: drought then flood, bad harvest, itching ears.

sentences.zh: 清明，晷長六尺二寸八分。

translations.literal: Pure Brightness: shadow length six chi two cun eight fen.
translations.idiomatic: Pure Brightness: noon shadow 6 chi 2 cun 8 fen.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，菽豆不熟，多病嚏、振寒

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, beans and legumes do not ripen; many sneezing, shivering cold.
translations.idiomatic: Late Pure Brightness: beans fail; sneezing and chills.

translations.literal: The gloss reads warm.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss marks warm fever alongside chill.

translations.literal: And copious diarrhea, end of list.
translations.idiomatic: and watery diarrhea.

sentences.zh: 未當至而至，多溫病、暴死。

translations.literal: If it ought not yet to arrive but does, many warm illnesses and sudden death.
translations.idiomatic: Early Pure Brightness: fevers and sudden deaths.

sentences.zh: 穀雨，晷長五尺三寸六分。

translations.literal: Grain Rain: shadow length five chi three cun six fen.
translations.idiomatic: Grain Rain: noon shadow 5 chi 3 cun 6 fen.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，水物雜稻等不為，多病疾瘧、振寒、霍亂。

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, aquatic crops and mixed rice do not succeed; many swift malaria, shivering cold, cholera.
translations.idiomatic: Late Grain Rain: wet-field crops and rice fail; malaria, chills, cholera.

sentences.zh: 未當至而至，老人多病氣腫。

translations.literal: If it ought not yet to arrive but does, old people mostly suffer qi swelling.
translations.idiomatic: Early Grain Rain: edema among the elderly.

sentences.zh: 立夏，晷長四尺三寸六分。

translations.literal: Summer Begins: shadow length four chi three cun six fen.
translations.idiomatic: Summer Begins: noon shadow 4 chi 3 cun 6 fen.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，旱，五穀傷，牛畜疾。

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, drought; the five grains are harmed; oxen and livestock fall ill.
translations.idiomatic: Late Summer Begins: drought, crop loss, sick cattle.

sentences.zh: 未當至而至，多病頭痛、腫嗌、喉痺。

translations.literal: If it ought not yet to arrive but does, many headache, swollen throat, throat blockage.
translations.idiomatic: Early Summer Begins: headache and throat ailments.

sentences.zh: 小滿，晷長三尺四寸。

translations.literal: Small Fullness: shadow length three chi four cun.
translations.idiomatic: Small Fullness: noon shadow 3 chi 4 cun.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，凶言，[國]有大喪，先水後旱，多病筋急、痺痛。

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, ill omens; the state has great mourning; first water then drought; many tight sinews and numb pain.
translations.idiomatic: Late Small Fullness: ill omens, royal bereavement, flood then drought, cramps and numb pain.

sentences.zh: 未當至而至，多熛、嗌腫。

translations.literal: If it ought not yet to arrive but does, many heatstroke and swollen throat.
translations.idiomatic: Early Small Fullness: heatstroke and throat swelling.

sentences.zh: 芒種，晷長二尺四寸四分。

translations.literal: Grain in Ear: shadow length two chi four cun four fen.
translations.idiomatic: Grain in Ear: noon shadow 2 chi 4 cun 4 fen.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，凶言，國有狂令。

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, ill omens; the state has reckless edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Late Grain in Ear: ill omens and lawless commands.

sentences.zh: 未當至而至，多病厥眩、頭痛。

translations.literal: If it ought not yet to arrive but does, many reversal vertigo and headache.
translations.idiomatic: Early Grain in Ear: fainting vertigo and headaches.

sentences.zh: 夏至，晷長一尺四寸八分。

translations.literal: Summer Solstice: shadow length one chi four cun eight fen.
translations.idiomatic: Summer Solstice: noon shadow 1 chi 4 cun 8 fen.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，國有大殃，旱，陰陽並傷，草木夏落，有大寒。

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, the state has great calamity; drought; Yin and Yang are both harmed; plants shed in summer; there is great cold.
translations.idiomatic: Late summer solstice: national disaster, drought, Yin-Yang imbalance, trees drop leaves in summer, untimely cold.

sentences.zh: 未當至而至，病眉腫。

translations.literal: If it ought not yet to arrive but does, illness of swollen eyebrows.
translations.idiomatic: Early summer solstice: swollen brows.

sentences.zh: 小暑，晷長二尺四寸四分。

translations.literal: Minor Heat: shadow length two chi four cun four fen.
translations.idiomatic: Minor Heat: noon shadow 2 chi 4 cun 4 fen.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，前小水，後小旱，有兵，多病洩注、腹痛。

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, first minor water, afterward minor drought; there is war; many diarrhea and belly pain.
translations.idiomatic: Late Minor Heat: brief wet then dry spell, warfare, dysentery and bellyache.

sentences.zh: 未當至而至，病臚腫。

translations.literal: If it ought not yet to arrive but does, illness of belly swelling.
translations.idiomatic: Early Minor Heat: abdominal swelling.

sentences.zh: 大暑，晷長三尺四寸。

translations.literal: Great Heat: shadow length three chi four cun.
translations.idiomatic: Great Heat: noon shadow 3 chi 4 cun.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，外兵作，來年饑，多病筋痺、匣痛。

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, foreign armies arise; famine next year; many sinew numbness and scapular pain.
translations.idiomatic: Late Great Heat: border war, next year's famine, sinew paralysis and thoracic pain.

sentences.zh: 未當至而至，多病脛痛、惡氣。

translations.literal: If it ought not yet to arrive but does, many shin pain and malign vapors.
translations.idiomatic: Early Great Heat: shin pain and foul miasma.

sentences.zh: 立秋，晷長四尺三寸六分。

translations.literal: Autumn Begins: shadow length four chi three cun six fen.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn Begins: noon shadow 4 chi 3 cun 6 fen.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，暴風為災，來年黍不為。

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, sudden wind becomes disaster; next year millet does not ripen.
translations.idiomatic: Late Autumn Begins: wind damage, failed millet next year.

sentences.zh: 未當至而至，多病咳上氣、咽腫。

translations.literal: If it ought not yet to arrive but does, many cough with upward qi and swollen throat.
translations.idiomatic: Early Autumn Begins: cough, panting, throat swellings.

sentences.zh: 處暑，晷長五尺三寸二分。

translations.literal: End of Heat: shadow length five chi three cun two fen.
translations.idiomatic: End of Heat: noon shadow 5 chi 3 cun 2 fen.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，國多浮令，兵起，來年麥不為。

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, the state has many hollow edicts; armies arise; next year wheat does not ripen.
translations.idiomatic: Late End of Heat: empty decrees, war, failed winter wheat.

sentences.zh: 未當至而至，病脹，耳熱不出行。

translations.literal: If it ought not yet to arrive but does, illness of distension, ears hot and unable to travel.
translations.idiomatic: Early End of Heat: bloating, burning ears, people keep indoors.

sentences.zh: 白靈，晷長六尺二寸八分。

translations.literal: White Spirit: shadow length six chi two cun eight fen.
translations.idiomatic: White Dew (written White Spirit in the manuscript): noon shadow 6 chi 2 cun 8 fen.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，多病痤、疽、洩。

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, many acne, abscesses, and diarrhea.
translations.idiomatic: Late White Dew: boils, abscesses, diarrhea.

sentences.zh: 未當至而至，多病水、腹閉疝瘕。

translations.literal: If it ought not yet to arrive but does, many water illnesses, blocked belly, hernia and masses.
translations.idiomatic: Early White Dew: edema, abdominal blockage, hernial masses.

sentences.zh: 秋分，晷長七尺二寸四分。

translations.literal: Autumn Equinox: shadow length seven chi two cun four fen.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn Equinox: noon shadow 7 chi 2 cun 4 fen.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，草木復榮，多病溫，悲心痛。

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, plants bloom again; many warm illnesses and grief heart pain.
translations.idiomatic: Late autumn equinox: untimely green growth, fevers, sorrowful chest pain.

sentences.zh: 未當至而至，多病匣鬲痛。

translations.literal: If it ought not yet to arrive but does, many pains in the chest and diaphragm.
translations.idiomatic: Early equinox: pain below the heart and across the diaphragm.

sentences.zh: 寒露，晷長八尺二寸。

translations.literal: Cold Dew: shadow length eight chi two cun.
translations.idiomatic: Cold Dew: noon shadow 8 chi 2 cun.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，來年谷不成，六畜鳥獸被殃，多病疝瘕、□痛。

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, next year grain does not ripen; domestic animals and birds suffer harm; many hernia-masses and missing pain.
translations.idiomatic: Late Cold Dew: crop failure, livestock plague, hernial lumps and rheumatic pain (character missing).

sentences.zh: 未當至而至，多病疢熱中。

translations.literal: If it ought not yet to arrive but does, many burning fevers within.
translations.idiomatic: Early Cold Dew: internal burning fevers.

sentences.zh: 霜降，晷長九尺一寸六分。

translations.literal: Frost's Descent: shadow length nine chi one cun six fen.
translations.idiomatic: Frost's Descent: noon shadow 9 chi 1 cun 6 fen.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，萬物大耗，年多大風，人病□痛。

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, the myriad things are greatly wasted; the year has great winds; people fall ill with missing pain.
translations.idiomatic: Late Frost's Descent: heavy loss of growth, gales, bodily pains (lacuna).

sentences.zh: 未當至而至，多病匣駿支滿。

translations.literal: If it ought not yet to arrive but does, many illnesses of chest binding and limb fullness.
translations.idiomatic: Early Frost's Descent: congested chest and swollen limbs (corrupt graphs in source).

sentences.zh: 立冬，晷長丈一寸二分。

translations.literal: Winter Begins: shadow length one zhang one cun two fen.
translations.idiomatic: Winter Begins: noon shadow 1 zhang 1 cun 2 fen.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，地氣不藏，來年立夏反寒，早旱，晚水，萬物不成。

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, earth qi does not store; next year Summer Begins turns cold; early drought, late flood; the myriad things do not ripen.
translations.idiomatic: Late Winter Begins: earth fails to close; next summer stays cold, drought then flood, crops fail.

sentences.zh: 未當至而至，多病臂掌痛。

translations.literal: If it ought not yet to arrive but does, many arm and palm pain.
translations.idiomatic: Early Winter Begins: sore arms and hands.

sentences.zh: 小雪，晷長一丈一尺八分。

translations.literal: Light Snow: shadow length one zhang one chi eight fen.
translations.idiomatic: Light Snow: noon shadow 1 zhang 1 chi 8 fen.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，來年蠶麥不成，多病恭腕痛。

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, next year silkworms and wheat do not succeed; many wrist pains.
translations.idiomatic: Late Light Snow: silk and wheat fail next year; sore wrists.

sentences.zh: 未當至而至，亦為多肘腋痛。

translations.literal: If it ought not yet to arrive but does, also many elbow and armpit pains.
translations.idiomatic: Early Light Snow: elbow and axilla pain.

sentences.zh: 大雪，晷長一丈二尺四分。

translations.literal: Great Snow: shadow length one zhang two chi four fen.
translations.idiomatic: Great Snow: noon shadow 1 zhang 2 chi 4 fen.

sentences.zh: 當至不至，溫氣洩，夏蝗蟲生，大水，多病少氣、五疸、水腫。

translations.literal: If it ought to arrive but does not, warm qi leaks out; summer locusts are born; great floods; many shortness of breath, five jaundices, edema.
translations.idiomatic: Late Great Snow: warmth escapes, summer locusts, floods, fatigue, jaundice, dropsy.

sentences.zh: 未當至而至，多病漢疽痛，應在芒種。

translations.literal: If it ought not yet to arrive but does, many gangrenous-sore pain; the response falls at Grain in Ear.
translations.idiomatic: Early Great Snow: ulcer pain answered at Grain in Ear.

sentences.zh: 月令章句曰：「周天三百六十五度四分度之一，分為十二次，日月之所躔也。

translations.literal: Monthly Ordinances with section headings says, in quotation marks: The full circuit of Heaven is three hundred sixty-five and one-quarter degrees; divided into twelve stations, these are where Sun and Moon tread.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong: the sky spans 365 degrees and one-quarter, split into twelve lunar stations along the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 地有十二分，王侯之所國也。

translations.literal: Earth has twelve divisions, the domains where kings and lords establish states.
translations.idiomatic: The realm below is mapped into twelve regions matching those stations.

sentences.zh: 每次三十

translations.literal: Each station thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Each celestial station spans thirty degrees of the circuit.

translations.literal: The gloss supplies the numeral two.
translations.idiomatic: Manuscript gloss: digit two in the fraction.

sentences.zh: 度三十

translations.literal: degrees thirty
translations.idiomatic: …thirty degrees…

translations.literal: The gloss supplies the numeral three.
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: three.

sentences.zh: [二]分之十四，日至其初為節，至其中為中氣。

translations.literal: [Two] fourteenths of a part; when the Sun reaches its beginning that is a seasonal node; when it reaches its middle that is a mid-qi.
translations.idiomatic: Each station spans 30°32′14″ (text split across glosses): the Sun’s entry marks a jie; its midpoint marks a zhong qi.

sentences.zh: 自危十度至壁

translations.literal: From Rooftop ten degrees to Wall
translations.idiomatic: From longitude Rooftop 10° through Wall

translations.literal: (eight)
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: eight.

sentences.zh: [九]度謂之豕韋之次，立春、驚蟄居之，衛之分野。

translations.literal: [nine] degrees is called the Encampment of Shiwei; Spring Begins and Waking of Insects dwell there; it is the field-allotment of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: …8°–9° of Wall—this is the Shiwei lodge; Spring Begins and Waking of Insects fall here; it maps to the region of Wei.

sentences.zh: 自壁

translations.literal: From Wall
translations.idiomatic: From Wall

translations.literal: (eight)
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: eight.

sentences.zh: [九]度至胃一度，謂之降婁之次，雨水、春分居之，魯之分野。

translations.literal: [nine] degrees to Stomach one degree is called the Encampment of Jianglou; Rain Water and Spring Equinox dwell there; it is the field-allotment of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: …Wall 8°–9° to Stomach 1° is Jianglou; Rain Water and the spring equinox belong to it; the allotment is Lu.

sentences.zh: 自胃一度至畢六度，謂之大梁之次，清明、穀雨居之，趙之分野。

translations.literal: From Stomach one degree to Net six degrees is called the Encampment of Daliang; Pure Brightness and Grain Rain dwell there; it is the field-allotment of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Stomach 1° to Net (Bi) 6° is Daliang; Pure Brightness and Grain Rain; allotment Zhao.

sentences.zh: 自畢六度至井十度，謂之實沉之次，立夏、小滿居之，晉之分野。

translations.literal: From Net six degrees to Well ten degrees is called the Encampment of Shichen; Summer Begins and Small Fullness dwell there; it is the field-allotment of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Net 6° to Well 10° is Shichen; Summer Begins and Small Fullness; allotment Jin.

sentences.zh: 自井十度至柳三度，謂之鶉首之次，芒種、夏至居之，秦之分野。

translations.literal: From Well ten degrees to Willow three degrees is called the Encampment of Chunshou; Grain in Ear and Summer Solstice dwell there; it is the field-allotment of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Well 10° to Willow 3° is Chunshou; Grain in Ear and summer solstice; allotment Qin.

sentences.zh: 自柳三度至張十二度，謂之鶉火之次，小暑、大暑居之，周之分野。

translations.literal: From Willow three degrees to Extended Net twelve degrees is called the Encampment of Chunhuo; Minor Heat and Great Heat dwell there; it is the field-allotment of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Willow 3° to Extended Net 12° is Chunhuo; the two heats; allotment Zhou.

sentences.zh: 自張十二度至軫六度，謂之鶉尾之次，立秋、處暑居之，楚之分野。

translations.literal: From Extended Net twelve degrees to Chariot six degrees is called the Encampment of Chunwei; Autumn Begins and End of Heat dwell there; it is the field-allotment of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Extended Net 12° to Chariot 6° is Chunwei; Autumn Begins and End of Heat; allotment Chu.

sentences.zh: 自軫六度至亢八度，謂之壽星之次，白露、秋分居之，鄭之分野。

translations.literal: From Chariot six degrees to Horn-Guard eight degrees is called the Encampment of Shouxing; White Dew and Autumn Equinox dwell there; it is the field-allotment of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chariot 6° to Horn-Guard 8° is Shouxing; White Dew and autumn equinox; allotment Zheng.

sentences.zh: 自亢八度至尾四度，謂之大火之次，寒露、霜降居之，宋之分野。

translations.literal: From Horn-Guard eight degrees to Tail four degrees is called the Encampment of Dahuo; Cold Dew and Frost’s Descent dwell there; it is the field-allotment of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Horn-Guard 8° to Tail 4° is Dahuo; Cold Dew and Frost’s Descent; allotment Song.

sentences.zh: 自尾四度至斗六度，謂之析木之次，立冬、小雪居之，燕之分野。

translations.literal: From Tail four degrees to Dipper six degrees is called the Encampment of Ximu; Winter Begins and Light Snow dwell there; it is the field-allotment of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Tail 4° to Dipper 6° is Ximu; Winter Begins and Light Snow; allotment Yan.

sentences.zh: 自斗六度至須女二度，謂之星紀之次，大雪、冬至居之，越之分野。

translations.literal: From Dipper six degrees to Girl two degrees is called the Encampment of Xingji; Great Snow and Winter Solstice dwell there; it is the field-allotment of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper 6° to Girl 2° is Xingji; Great Snow and winter solstice; allotment Yue.

sentences.zh: 自須女二度至危十度，謂之玄枵之次，小寒、大寒居之，齊之分野。」

translations.literal: From Girl two degrees to Rooftop ten degrees is called the Encampment of Xuanxiao; Minor Cold and Great Cold dwell there; it is the field-allotment of Qi, end quotation.
translations.idiomatic: Girl 2° to Rooftop 10° is Xuanxiao; Minor and Great Cold; allotment Qi—closing Cai Yong’s quotation.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕分星次度數與皇甫謐不同，兼明氣節所在，故載焉。

translations.literal: Cai Yong’s division of stations and degree-numbers differs from Huangfu Mi’s; because he also clarifies where qi nodes fall, it is recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong’s celestial-field boundaries disagree with Huangfu Mi’s; since he ties in the solar terms, his version is included.

sentences.zh: 謐所列在郡國志。

translations.literal: What Mi listed is in the Treatise on Commanderies and States.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Mi’s table appears in the geography monograph.

sentences.zh: 中星以日所在為正，日行四歲乃終，置所求年二十四氣小余四之，如法為少、大，余不盡，三之，如法為強、弱，以減節氣□明中星，而各定矣。

translations.literal: Culminating stars take the Sun’s place as correct; the Sun’s motion completes in four years; set the twenty-four qi minor remainders of the year sought, multiply by four; according to the rule they make lesser or greater; what remains not exhausted, multiply by three; according to the rule they make strong or weak; subtract from the solar term’s twilight culminating stars, and each is fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Meridian stars are keyed to solar longitude; the Sun’s cycle closes in four years—quadruple the year’s qi fractions, reduce by the calendrical rule to strong/weak quarter-degrees, and subtract from the tabulated culminations to update the almanac.

sentences.zh: 強，正；

translations.literal: Strong: correct;
translations.idiomatic: A ‘strong’ label counts as positive correction.

sentences.zh: 弱，

translations.literal: weak,
translations.idiomatic: A ‘weak’ label

translations.literal: (straight)
translations.idiomatic: The gloss reads ‘straight’ versus oblique.

sentences.zh: [負]也。

translations.literal: [negative].
translations.idiomatic: …counts as negative offset.

sentences.zh: 其強弱相減，同名相去，異名從之。

translations.literal: Subtract strong and weak from each other; same name removes, different name follows.
translations.idiomatic: Combine corrections: like signs subtract, unlike signs add.

sentences.zh: 從強進少為弱，從弱退少而強。

translations.literal: Following strong, advance lesser to weak; following weak, retreat lesser to strong.
translations.idiomatic: Carry overflows from strong into weak ranks and vice versa per the rod rules.

sentences.zh: 從上元太歲在庚辰以來，盡熹平三年，歲在甲寅，積九千四百五十五歲也[19]。

translations.literal: From the high yuan when Grand Year stood at gengchen down to the third year of Xiping, when the year is jiayin, the accumulated count is nine thousand four hundred fifty-five years [19].
translations.idiomatic: From the epoch (Tai-sui at gengchen) to Xiping 3 (jiayin) is 9,455 years [19].

sentences.zh: 論曰：易有太極，是生兩儀。

translations.literal: The discussion says: In the Changes there is the Great Ultimate; it produces the Two Modes.
translations.idiomatic: The essay opens: the Great Ultimate begets Yin and Yang.

sentences.zh: 兩儀之分尚矣，乃有皇犧。

translations.literal: The division of the Two Modes is ancient; then there was Sovereign Fu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yin and Yang parted, culture begins with Fu Xi.

sentences.zh: 皇犧之有天下也，未有書計。

translations.literal: When Sovereign Fu Xi possessed All under Heaven, there were not yet writing or reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Under Fu Xi there was neither script nor arithmetic.

sentences.zh: 歷載彌久，暨於黃帝，班示文章，重黎記注，像應著名，始終相驗，准度追元，乃立歷數。

translations.literal: Years and records grew ever older; reaching the Yellow Emperor, he displayed writing, Chong and Li kept registers, models matched and names were fixed, beginning and end mutually verified, standards traced to the origin—then calendrical numbers were established.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yellow Emperor texts appeared, Chong and Li kept celestial logs, instruments matched heaven, and only then could the calendar be founded.

sentences.zh: 天難諶斯，是以五、三迄於來今，各有改作，不通用。

translations.literal: Heaven is hard to trust in this; therefore from the Five Thearchs and Three Ages down to the present, each age has reformed the system; they are not universally interchangeable.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s measure is subtle, so every dynasty from the Five Thearchs onward has revised the calendar—no single system serves all ages.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：象因物生，數本杪曶。

translations.literal: Praise says: Images arise from things; numbers root in the subtle instant.
