sentences.zh: 三０七七頁一三行室八度二十八分進三「進三」原作「退三」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3077, line 13: Hall eight degrees twenty-eight fen advance three—‘advance three’ originally ‘retreat three,’ miswritten.
translations.idiomatic: The equatorial conversion for Hall requires an advance of three, not a retreat; the direction was inverted in transmission.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本「退」作「進」，逕據改。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian says Li’s edition reads ‘advance’ for ‘retreat’—emended directly.
translations.idiomatic: 進 for 退.

sentences.zh: 三０七七頁一三行箕大弱退三「箕」下原有大字「六」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3077, line 13: Winnowing Basket lesser-weak retreat three—below ‘Winnowing Basket’ the original had a large graph ‘six,’ miswritten.
translations.idiomatic: Delete spurious 六.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本無「六」字，逕據刪。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition lacks the character 「六」 and deletes it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianqian notes the Li recension has no 六 here; the text drops the character accordingly.

sentences.zh: 三０七八頁一行八十九強「強」原作「少強」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3078, line 1: eighty-nine 強: 「強」 was originally written 「少強」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: the manuscript wrongly read 少強 where the table should show 強 alone for the eighty-ninth degree mark.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本無「少」字，徑據刪。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition lacks the character 「少」 and deletes it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianqian: the Li text has no 少; the redundant character is removed.

sentences.zh: 三０七八頁一行斗十一弱退二「弱」原作「強」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3078, line 1, Dipper eleven 弱 retreat two: 「弱」 was originally written 「強」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Collation fixes Dipper 11: the weak grade was misprinted as 強.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本作「弱」，徑據改。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition reads 「弱」 and emends to it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: The reading 弱 is adopted from the Li edition.

sentences.zh: 三０七八頁二行胃一度十七分退一「退一」原作「退二」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3078, line 2: Stomach one degree seventeen fen retreat one: 「退一」 was originally written 「退二」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Stomach’s motion is corrected from retreat two to retreat one.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本作「退一」，逕據改。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition reads 「退一」 and emends to it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: Retreat one is the reading taken from the Li edition.

sentences.zh: 三０七八頁二行星四大進一「進」下原脫「一」字，王先謙謂李本「進」下有「一」字，逕據補。

translations.literal: Page 3078, line 2: planet four great advance one: below 「進」 the text originally omitted the character 「一」; Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition has 「一」 after 「進」, and it is supplied outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: The lacuna after 進 is filled with 一 to match the Li edition’s planet entry.

sentences.zh: 三０七八頁三行張十七進一「進一」原斗「進二」，逕據汲本改正。

translations.literal: Page 3078, line 3: Extended Net seventeen advance one: 「進一」 was originally confused with 「進二」, and is corrected per the Ji edition.
translations.idiomatic: Extended Net’s advance is set to 進一, not 進二, following the Ji imprint.

sentences.zh: 按：王先謙謂李本作「大進一」。

translations.literal: Comment: Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition reads 「大進一」.
translations.idiomatic: Wang notes the Li text actually has 大進一 for this line.

sentences.zh: 三０七八頁四行畢六度「六」原作「八」，鬥，徑據汲本改正。

translations.literal: Page 3078, line 4: Net six degrees: 「六」 was originally written 「八」, edition conflict, corrected per the Ji edition.
translations.idiomatic: Net’s width is emended from eight to six degrees per the Ji edition.

sentences.zh: 三０七八頁四行女十少進一「進」原作「弱」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3078, line 4: Girl ten 少 advance one: 「進」 was originally written 「弱」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: The motion label is 進, not the grade 弱, for Girl ten 少.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本「弱」作「進」，逕據改。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that in the Li edition 「弱」 is written 「進」 and emends to it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: The Li edition’s 進 replaces the erroneous 弱.

sentences.zh: 三０七八頁五行角大弱「大」原作「六」，大字，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3078, line 5: Horn great 弱: 「大」 was originally written 「六」, large character, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: the large-script 大 grade was misprinted as the numeral 六.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本「六」作「大」，小字，逕據改。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that in the Li edition 「六」 is written 「大」, small character, and emends to it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: The small-script numeral is corrected to the grade 大 per Li.

sentences.zh: 三０七八頁七行室十二少弱進三「進三」原作「退三」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3078, line 7: Rooftop twelve 少弱 advance three: 「進三」 was originally written 「退三」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Rooftop’s motion is advance three, not retreat three.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本作「進三」，逕據改。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition reads 「進三」 and emends to it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: Advance three is adopted from the Li edition.

sentences.zh: 三０七八頁九行星四度二分進一「二分進一」原作「三分進二」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3078, line 9: planet four degrees two fen advance one: 「二分進一」 was originally written 「三分進二」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: The planet line is corrected to two fen and advance one.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本作「二分進一」，逕據改。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition reads 「二分進一」 and emends to it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rui’s 二分進一 reading is accepted.

sentences.zh: 三０七八頁一０行胃九大弱退一「退一」原作「退二」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3078, line 10: Stomach nine great 弱 retreat one: 「退一」 was originally written 「退二」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Stomach nine’s retreat is one, not two.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本作「退一」，逕據改。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition reads 「退一」 and emends to it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: Retreat one is the Li edition reading.

sentences.zh: 三０七八頁一一行翼九度十六分進二「進二」原作「退二」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3078, line 11: Wings nine degrees sixteen fen advance two: 「進二」 was originally written 「退二」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Wings’ motion is advance two, not retreat two.

sentences.zh: 李本作「進一」，亦誤。

translations.literal: The Li edition reads 「進一」, which is also wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Li text’s 進一 is rejected as incorrect here.

sentences.zh: 依算理應為「進二」，今徑改。

translations.literal: According to computational principle it ought to be 「進二」, and it is emended directly to that.
translations.idiomatic: The arithmetic requires 進二, so the text is set to that value.

sentences.zh: 三０七八頁一一行斗十少退二「退」下原脫「二」字，王先謙謂李本作「退二」，徑據補。

translations.literal: Page 3078, line 11: Dipper ten 少 retreat two: below 「退」 the text originally omitted the character 「二」; Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition reads 「退二」, and it is supplied outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: The missing 二 after 退 is restored from the Li edition.

sentences.zh: 三０七八頁一二行軫六度二十三分進一「進一」原作「退一」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3078, line 12: Chariot End six degrees twenty-three fen advance one: 「進一」 was originally written 「退一」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Chariot End advances one fen, not retreats.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本作「進一」，逕據改。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition reads 「進一」 and emends to it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: Advance one is read from the Li edition.

sentences.zh: 三０七八頁一二行斗二十一強退二「退」下原脫一字。

translations.literal: Page 3078, line 12: Dipper twenty-one 強 retreat two: below 「退」 one character was originally missing.
translations.idiomatic: Collation flags a lacuna after 退 on the Dipper twenty-one 強 line.

sentences.zh: 汲本、殿本作「退一」，鬥。

translations.literal: The Ji edition and the palace edition read 「退一」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Dian prints have 退一, which disagrees with the preferred reading.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本作「退二」，逕據補。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition reads 「退二」 and supplies it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: 退二 is supplied per Wang, following the Li edition.

sentences.zh: 三０七八頁一四行亢八度五分退一「退一」原作「退三」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3078, line 14: Neck eight degrees five fen retreat one: 「退一」 was originally written 「退三」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Neck’s retreat is one fen, not three.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本作「退一」，逕據改。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition reads 「退一」 and emends to it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: The Li edition’s 退一 is adopted.

sentences.zh: 三０七八頁一四行九十六大強「大強」原作「少強」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3078, line 14: ninety-six great 強: 「大強」 was originally written 「少強」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: The grade is emended from 少強 to 大強.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本作「大強」，逕據改。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition reads 「大強」 and emends to it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: 大強 is the Li edition’s grade reading.

sentences.zh: 三０七九頁一行氐十四度十二分退二「十二分」原作「十三分」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3079, line 1: Root fourteen degrees twelve fen retreat two: 「十二分」 was originally written 「十三分」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Root’s fraction is twelve fen, not thirteen.

sentences.zh: 錢大昕謂「三」當作「二」，王先謙謂李本作「十二分」，逕據改。

translations.literal: Qian Daxin states that 「三」 ought to be 「二」; Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition reads 「十二分」 and emends to it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: Qian emends the tens digit; Wang confirms 十二分 from the Li text.

sentences.zh: 三０七九頁一行虛六大進二「進二」原作「進一」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3079, line 1: Emptiness six great advance two: 「進二」 was originally written 「進一」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Emptiness six advances two, not one.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本作「進二」，逕據改。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition reads 「進二」 and emends to it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: Advance two is taken from the Li edition.

sentences.zh: 三０七九頁二行尾四度「尾」原作「房」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3079, line 2: Tail four degrees: 「尾」 was originally written 「房」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: The lodge name is Tail (尾), not Room (房).

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本作「尾」，逕據改。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition reads 「尾」 and emends to it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: 尾 is the Li edition’s lodge label.

sentences.zh: 三０七九頁二行丈「丈」下原有「四寸二分」四字。

translations.literal: Page 3079, line 2: after the character 「丈」 the text originally carried the four characters 「四寸二分」.
translations.idiomatic: The manuscript appended 四寸二分 after 丈 in the gnomon entry.

sentences.zh: 集解引李銳說，謂案祖沖之術二至晷景與此同。

translations.literal: The Collected Commentary cites Li Rui’s argument that, by Zu Chongzhi’s method, the solstitial shadow lengths here match.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rui shows Zu Chongzhi’s solstice shadows agree with this passage.

sentences.zh: 其至前後各氣晷景，以此至前後晷景兩兩相加，折半得之。

translations.literal: For each solar term’s gnomon shadow before and after the solstice, take the solstitial shadows before and after, add the pairs term by term, and halve the sum to obtain the value.
translations.idiomatic: Li explains how to derive mid-season shadows by averaging paired solstice-adjacent readings.

sentences.zh: 如此術大雪景丈二尺五寸六分，小寒景二尺三寸，相加半之，得沖之術大雪、小寒景一丈二尺四寸三分是也。

translations.literal: Thus by this method Major Snow’s shadow is one zhang two chi five cun six fen, and Minor Cold’s is two chi three cun; adding and halving yields Zu Chongzhi’s Major Snow and Minor Cold shadow of one zhang two chi four cun three fen.
translations.idiomatic: The worked example matches Zu’s figures for Major Snow and Minor Cold when averaged correctly.

sentences.zh: 覆檢此文，惟立冬一氣不合。

translations.literal: On re-examination of this passage, only the Beginning of Winter term fails to fit.
translations.idiomatic: Only Lìdōng’s shadow line is inconsistent with the rest.

sentences.zh: 案祖沖之稱四分志立冬中景長一丈，立春中景九尺六寸，相加半之，得九尺八寸，與沖之術立春、立冬景正合。

translations.literal: For Zu Chongzhi states in the Quarter-day Treatise that at mid-Lìdōng the shadow is one zhang, and at mid-Lìchūn nine chi six cun; adding and halving yields nine chi eight cun, which matches Zu’s method for Lìchūn and Lìdōng shadows.
translations.idiomatic: Zu’s own mid-term values for winter and spring solstitial pairs average to his Lìchūn/Lìdōng shadows.

sentences.zh: 然則此文立冬晷景丈四寸二分，誤衍「四寸二分」四字耳。

translations.literal: Therefore in this text the Lìdōng gnomon shadow of one zhang four cun two fen merely has the four characters 「四寸二分」 erroneously appended.
translations.idiomatic: The extra 四寸二分 after 丈 is a dittography; the true reading is one zhang flat.

sentences.zh: 今徑據刪。

translations.literal: It is now deleted outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: The spurious 四寸二分 is struck from the text.

sentences.zh: 三０七九頁二行張十五大強進一「進一」原作「進二」，汲本無「進一」二字。

translations.literal: Page 3079, line 2: Extended Net fifteen great 強 advance one: 「進一」 was originally written 「進二」, and the Ji edition lacks the two characters 「進一」.
translations.idiomatic: Collation balances Extended Net’s 進一 against Ji (which omits it) and other witnesses.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本多「進一」二字，殿本同，逕據改。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition has the extra two characters 「進一」, the palace edition agrees, and it is emended to that reading outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: Wang keeps 進一, which Li and Dian share against the Ji lacuna.

sentences.zh: 三０七九頁三行室三原作「室二」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3079, line 3: Rooftop three was originally written 「室二」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: The Rooftop count is three, not two.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本「室二」作「室三」，逕據改。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that in the Li edition 「室二」 is written 「室三」 and emends to it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: Li’s 室三 is adopted for Rooftop.

sentences.zh: 三０七九頁四行斗六度一分退二「退二」原作「退三」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3079, line 4: Dipper six degrees one fen retreat two: 「退二」 was originally written 「退三」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper retreats two fen, not three.

sentences.zh: 王先謙謂李本作「退二」，逕據改。

translations.literal: Wang Xianqian states that the Li edition reads 「退二」 and emends to it outright on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: Retreat two follows the Li edition.

sentences.zh: 三０七九頁四行軫十五弱進一「弱」原作「少強」，鬥。

translations.literal: Page 3079, line 4: Chariot End fifteen 弱 advance one: 「弱」 was originally written 「少強」, edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: The grade should be 弱, not 少強.

sentences.zh: 李本作「少弱」，亦鬥。

translations.literal: The Li edition reads 「少弱」, which is also an edition conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Li’s 少弱 is likewise rejected.

sentences.zh: 依算理應作「弱」，逕改。

translations.literal: According to computational principle it ought to read 「弱」, and it is emended directly to that.
translations.idiomatic: Arithmetic requires the plain grade 弱.

sentences.zh: 三０七九頁一五行振寒

translations.literal: Page 3079, line 15: 振寒.
translations.idiomatic: Lemma 振寒 in the seasonal list (collation block).
Gloss marking 振 as related to 溫 in the apparatus.

sentences.zh: [洞]洩據汲本、殿本改。

translations.literal: [洞]洩: emended per the Ji edition and the palace edition.
translations.idiomatic: The compound is read 洞洩 per Ji and Dian witnesses.

sentences.zh: 三０八０頁二行[國]有大喪據汲本、殿本補。

translations.literal: Page 3080, line 2: [國] there is great mourning: supplied per the Ji edition and the palace edition.
translations.idiomatic: The phrase 國有大喪 is restored from Ji and Dian.

sentences.zh: 三０八０頁一四行五疸「疸」原斗「疽」，逕據殿本、集解本改正。

translations.literal: Page 3080, line 14: five 疸: 「疸」 was originally confused with 「疽」, corrected per the palace edition and the Collected Commentary edition.
translations.idiomatic: 疸 replaces the erroneous 疽 in the five-illness list.

sentences.zh: 三０八０頁一六行每次三十

translations.literal: Page 3080, line 16: each time thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Lemma: thirty each interval.
Gloss digit two in the fractional apparatus.

sentences.zh: 度三十

translations.literal: degrees thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Continuation: thirty degrees.
Gloss digit three.

sentences.zh: [二]分之十四據集解引錢大昕說刪改。

translations.literal: [二] fourteen parts thereof: emended per Qian Daxin as cited in the Collected Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Qian’s emendation yields two fourteenths for the fraction.

sentences.zh: 三０八０頁一六行自危十度至壁

translations.literal: Page 3080, line 16: from Emptiness ten degrees to Wall.
translations.idiomatic: Span lemma: Emptiness 10° through Wall.
Gloss digit eight.

sentences.zh: [九]度據集解引錢大昕說改。

translations.literal: [九] degrees: emended per Qian Daxin as cited in the Collected Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Wall’s endpoint is nine degrees per Qian.

sentences.zh: 下「自壁八度至胃一度」同。

translations.literal: Below, 「from Wall eight degrees to Stomach one degree」 is the same.
translations.idiomatic: The same emendation applies to the following Wall-to-Stomach span.

sentences.zh: 三０八０頁一七行立春驚蟄居之按：殿本「驚蟄」作「雨水」，下「雨水」作「驚蟄」。

translations.literal: Page 3080, line 17: Lìchūn and Jīngzhé occupy it—comment: in the palace edition 「驚蟄」 reads 「雨水」, and below 「雨水」 reads 「驚蟄」.
translations.idiomatic: Dian transposes the Jīngzhé and Yǔshuǐ labels relative to the received text.

sentences.zh: 集解引錢大昕說，謂此以驚蟄為正月中氣，雨水為二月節，依古法也。

translations.literal: The Collected Commentary cites Qian Daxin’s argument that here Jīngzhé is the second-month mid qi and Yǔshuǐ the second-month solar term, following ancient usage.
translations.idiomatic: Qian explains the old ordering: Jīngzhé as mid-month qi, Yǔshuǐ as the term.

sentences.zh: 四分術以雨水為正月中氣。

translations.literal: The Quarter-day system takes Yǔshuǐ as the second-month mid qi.
translations.idiomatic: The Quarter-day calendar instead places Yǔshuǐ in the mid-qi slot.

sentences.zh: 三０八一頁一行清明穀雨居之集解引盧文弨說，謂清明穀雨當互易。

translations.literal: Page 3081, line 1: Qīngmíng and Gǔyǔ occupy it—the Collected Commentary cites Lu Wenchao’s argument that Qīngmíng and Gǔyǔ ought to be transposed.
translations.idiomatic: Lu argues Qīngmíng and Gǔyǔ should swap positions.

sentences.zh: 今按：證以月令問答，惟驚蟄、雨水用三統，余皆用四分，易之非是。

translations.literal: Now comment: verified against the Monthly Ordinances dialogue, only Jīngzhé and Yǔshuǐ follow the Triple Concordance system; all the rest follow the Quarter-day system—transposing them would be wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The editor rejects Lu’s swap: only the rain terms use Triple Concordance; the rest match Quarter-day.

sentences.zh: 三０八一頁一０行強正弱

translations.literal: Page 3081, line 10: 強 rectifies 弱.
translations.idiomatic: Lemma on strong versus weak gradings.
Gloss character 直 in the note.

sentences.zh: [負]也集解引李銳說，謂「直」當作「負」，負猶背也。

translations.literal: [負] also: the Collected Commentary cites Li Rui’s argument that 「直」 ought to be 「負」, and 負 means ‘turned away’ (like the back).
translations.idiomatic: Li Rui reads 負 for 直, explaining 負 as ‘opposite / backs away’.

sentences.zh: 今據改。

translations.literal: It is now emended on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: The text adopts 負 per Li Rui.

sentences.zh: 三０八二頁七行追太初前

translations.literal: Page 3082, line 7: tracing back before the Grand Inception.
translations.idiomatic: Lemma opening the retrograde count from Grand Inception.
Gloss: the character 世 in the manuscript line.

sentences.zh: [卅]一元據集解引盧文弨說改。

translations.literal: [卅] one cycle: emended per Lu Wenchao as cited in the Collected Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Lu emends 世 to 卅 for ‘thirty’ cycles.

sentences.zh: 按：前志謂太初元年距上元十四萬三千一百二十七歲，正為太初前卅一元，「卅」與「世」形近而鬥。

translations.literal: Comment: the preceding Treatise states that Grand Inception year 1 stands 143,127 years from the high origin—exactly thirty-one cycles before Grand Inception, and 「卅」 was confused with 「世」 because the graphs resemble each other.
translations.idiomatic: The arithmetic matches thirty-one 元 cycles; 世 is a graphic error for 卅.

sentences.zh: 三０八二頁九行追漢

translations.literal: Page 3082, line 9: tracing back the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Lemma for the Han-era retrojection.
Gloss digit three.

sentences.zh: [四]十五年庚辰之歲據集解引錢大昕說改。

translations.literal: [四] fifteen years, the gēngchén year: emended per Qian Daxin as cited in the Collected Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Qian corrects the count to forty-five years to the gēngchén year.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁二行趨走目下遂竟端右出相好藩按：集解引惠棟說，謂邕集「目」作「陛」，「竟」作「由」，「好」作「外」。

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 2: hastening below the eyes then reaching the end, the right emerges in mutual favor at the frontier—comment: the Collected Commentary cites Hui Dong’s argument that in Cai Yong’s collected works 「目」 reads 「陛」, 「竟」 reads 「由」, and 「好」 reads 「外」.
translations.idiomatic: Hui Dong quotes variant diction from Cai Yong’s anthology for this memorial phrase.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁三行一旦

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 3: once.
translations.idiomatic: Lemma 一旦.
Gloss character 披.

sentences.zh: [被]章據汲本、殿本改。

translations.literal: [被] the edict: emended per the Ji edition and the palace edition.
translations.idiomatic: 被章 ‘receive the rescript’ replaces 披 per standard editions.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁四行非臣無狀所敢[復]望據汲本、殿本補。

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 4: it is not what your servant’s unworthiness would dare [again] to hope for—supplied per the Ji edition and the palace edition.
translations.idiomatic: 復 is added in 非臣無狀所敢復望 per Ji and Dian.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁五行[減罪]一等「一等」上疑有脫文，今據嚴可均輯全後漢文補「減罪」二字。

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 5: [reduce the crime] one grade—above 「一等」 the text is suspected of lacuna; 「減罪」 two characters are now supplied from Yan Kejun’s anthology of Later Han prose.
translations.idiomatic: The editor inserts 減罪 before 一等 following Yan’s reconstruction.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁六行[邕為]郡縣促遣集解引盧文弨說，謂脫「邕為」二字。

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 6: [Yong was] urged on by commandery and county officials—the Collected Commentary cites Lu Wenchao’s argument that the two characters 「邕為」 are missing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu supplies 邕為 before 郡縣促遣.

sentences.zh: 今據補。

translations.literal: They are now supplied on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: 邕為 is added to the sentence.

sentences.zh: 按：惠棟補注謂「郡縣」上邕集有「邕為」二字。

translations.literal: Comment: Hui Dong’s supplementary note states that above 「郡縣」 Cai Yong’s anthology has the two characters 「邕為」.
translations.idiomatic: Hui Dong’s gloss confirms Yong’s collection reads 邕為郡縣.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁六行□於吏手按：集解引惠棟說，謂「□」邕集作「迫」。

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 6: □ in the clerks’ hands—comment: the Collected Commentary cites Hui Dong’s argument that the lacuna 「□」 reads 「迫」 in Cai Yong’s anthology.
translations.idiomatic: Hui Dong fills the damaged character with 迫 per Cai Yong’s parallel text.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁七行但[懷]愚心據集解引盧文弨說補。

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 7: only [cherish] a foolish heart—supplied per Lu Wenchao as cited in the Collected Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: 懷 is supplied in 但懷愚心 per Lu.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁八行略以所有舊事[與臣]據集解引盧文弨說補。

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 8: briefly using what old matters I have [with your servant]—supplied per Lu Wenchao as cited in the Collected Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: 與臣 is added after 舊事 per Lu’s supplement.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁一０行

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 10.
translations.idiomatic: Collation header only: apparatus continues on page 3083, line 10.

sentences.zh: (所使元順)

translations.literal: (The phrase 「所使元順」).
translations.idiomatic: Apparatus gloss marking the four-character phrase 所使元順 for emendation.

sentences.zh: [其]難者皆以付臣集解引惠棟說，謂邕集無「所使元順」四字，有「其」字。

translations.literal: [As for] the difficult parts, all were entrusted to your servant—the Collected Commentary cites Hui Dong’s argument that Cai Yong’s collected works lack the four characters 「所使元順」 and have the character 「其」 instead.
translations.idiomatic: Hui Dong: Yong’s anthology reads 其難者皆以付臣 without 所使元順.

sentences.zh: 今據改。

translations.literal: It is now emended on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: The text is adjusted to match Cai Yong’s anthology.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁一一行請太

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 11: request the Grand.
translations.idiomatic: Lemma opening the line ‘request the Grand…’ in the memorial.

translations.literal: (Preceptor).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: the character grouping 師 (as in 太師).

sentences.zh: [史]舊注據集解引盧文弨說改。

translations.literal: [Astrologer] old commentary: emended per Lu Wenchao as cited in the Collected Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: The title is emended to 太史 ‘Grand Astrologer,’ not 太師.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁一二行尋繹適有頭角集解引盧文弨說，謂「尋繹」下脫「度數」二字。

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 12: tracing it out, there happens to be a beginning—the Collected Commentary cites Lu Wenchao’s argument that below 「尋繹」 the two characters 「度數」 are missing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu notes a lacuna after 尋繹: supply 度數.

sentences.zh: 按：如盧說增「度數」二字，則當於「尋繹度數」絕句。

translations.literal: Comment: if one adds the two characters 「度數」 per Lu’s view, the sentence should break after 「尋繹度數」.
translations.idiomatic: With 尋繹度數 supplied, the pause falls after that phrase.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁一二行

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 12.
translations.idiomatic: Collation header for line 12 on page 3083.

translations.literal: (Then).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: manuscript 遂.

sentences.zh: [逐]放邊野集解引惠棟說，謂邕集「遂」作「逐」。

translations.literal: [Drive] out to the frontier wilds—the Collected Commentary cites Hui Dong’s argument that in Cai Yong’s collected works 「遂」 is written 「逐」.
translations.idiomatic: 逐放 ‘drive into exile’ replaces 遂 per Yong’s text.

sentences.zh: 今據改。

translations.literal: It is now emended on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: 遂 is changed to 逐.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁一三行

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 13.
translations.idiomatic: Collation header for line 13 on page 3083.

translations.literal: (Therefore).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: 故 as a mistaken character.

sentences.zh: [胡]廣所校據汲本、殿本改。

translations.literal: [Hu] Guang’s collation: emended per the Ji edition and the palace edition.
translations.idiomatic: 胡廣 is the correct name, not 故.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁一三行不能違望按：集解引盧文弨說，謂「違望」一作「自達」。

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 13: unable to go against what is hoped—comment: the Collected Commentary cites Lu Wenchao’s argument that 「違望」 has one variant reading 「自達」.
translations.idiomatic: Lu records the variant 自達 for 違望.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁一五行不

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 15: not.
translations.idiomatic: Lemma fragment before the emended phrase.

sentences.zh: (言四)

translations.literal: (speak of the four).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: erroneous 言四 in the manuscript.

sentences.zh: [意西]夷相與合謀據集解引盧文弨說改。

translations.literal: [the western] barbarians plotting together—emended per Lu Wenchao as cited in the Collected Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: The clause is restored as 意西夷相與合謀 per Lu.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁一六行謹先顛踣按：集解引惠棟說，謂「謹」邕集作「恐」。

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 16: respectfully I first stumble and fall—comment: the Collected Commentary cites Hui Dong’s argument that 「謹」 in Cai Yong’s collected works is written 「恐」.
translations.idiomatic: Hui Dong: Yong’s text has 恐先颠踣 rather than 謹.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁一六行臣欲

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 16: your servant wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Lemma opening ‘your servant wishes…’.

translations.literal: (compile).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: 制 as editorial ‘compile’ (for deletion context).

sentences.zh: 刪定者一據集解引盧文弨說刪。

translations.literal: ‘one who deletes and fixes’—deleted per Lu Wenchao as cited in the Collected Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Lu strikes the phrase 刪定者一 as spurious.

sentences.zh: 三０八三頁一七行臣欲著者

translations.literal: Page 3083, line 17: what your servant wishes to write.
translations.idiomatic: Lemma: the works Yong proposes to compose.

translations.literal: (three).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss digit three.

sentences.zh: [五]集解引惠棟說，謂「三」邕集作「五」。

translations.literal: [five]—the Collected Commentary cites Hui Dong’s argument that 「三」 in Cai Yong’s collected works is written 「五」.
translations.idiomatic: Hui Dong: five works in Yong’s anthology, not three.

sentences.zh: 盧文弨亦謂「三」當作「五」。

translations.literal: Lu Wenchao also states that 「三」 ought to be 「五」.
translations.idiomatic: Lu agrees the count should be five.

sentences.zh: 今據改。

translations.literal: It is now emended on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: The numeral is changed from three to five.

sentences.zh: 顓頊曰重黎。

translations.literal: Zhuanxu called them Chong and Li.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhuanxu the calendrical officials were Chong and Li.

sentences.zh: 唐﹑虞﹑夏﹑商曰羲和。

translations.literal: Under Tang, Yu, Xia, and Shang they were called Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages styled the calendar office Xihe.

sentences.zh: 月令章句曰：「帝舜叶時月正日，湯、武革命，治歷明時。

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances commentary says: ‘Emperor Shun harmonized the seasons, months, and the rectified first day; Tang and Wu received the mandate of revolution and regulated the calendar to clarify the seasons.’
translations.idiomatic: The gloss ties Shun’s harmonization to the Shang founders’ calendar reform.

sentences.zh: 言承平者叶之，承亂者革之。」

translations.literal: It means: in peaceful succession one harmonizes; in times of turmoil one reforms.’
translations.idiomatic: Peace calls for adjustment; upheaval calls for a new system.

sentences.zh: 即是起捨合朔。

translations.literal: That is how one sets the new moon and unites conjunctions (起捨合朔).
translations.idiomatic: The commentator explains aligning intercalation with lunation (合朔).

sentences.zh: 月令章句曰：「紀，還復故歷。」

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances commentary says: ‘A ji cycle means returning to the former calendar.’
translations.idiomatic: Ji marks a return to the prior calendrical baseline.

sentences.zh: 月令章句曰：「七十六歲為蔀首。」

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances commentary says: ‘Seventy-six years form the head of a bu.’
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-six years begin a bu period in this scheme.

sentences.zh: 月令章句曰：「十九歲七閏月為一章。」

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances commentary says: ‘Nineteen years and seven intercalary months form one zhang.’
translations.idiomatic: The Metonic-style rule: nineteen years with seven leap months per zhang.

sentences.zh: 月令章句：「孟春以立春為節，驚蟄為中。

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances commentary: ‘In the first month of spring, Beginning of Spring is the solar term and Awakening of Insects is the mid qi.’
translations.idiomatic: First spring month: Lìchūn as term, Jīngzhé as mid-month qi.

sentences.zh: 中必在其月，節不必在其月。

translations.literal: The mid qi must fall within its month; the solar term need not fall within its month.
translations.idiomatic: Mid qi stays tied to its civil month; terms may spill across months.

sentences.zh: 據孟春之驚蟄在十六日以後，立春在正月；

translations.literal: According to the case where Awakening of Insects in the first month of spring falls after the sixteenth day, Beginning of Spring falls in the first month;
translations.idiomatic: If Jīngzhé is late in the month, Lìchūn stays in month one.

sentences.zh: 驚蟄在十五日以前，立春在往年十二月。」

translations.literal: if Awakening of Insects falls before the fifteenth day, Beginning of Spring falls in the twelfth month of the previous year.’
translations.idiomatic: If Jīngzhé is early, Lìchūn shifts back into the prior year’s twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 四分退二

translations.literal: Quarter-day: retreat two.
translations.idiomatic: Table tag: Quarter-day system, retreat two (步).

sentences.zh: 張衡渾儀曰：「赤道橫帶渾天之腹，去極九十一度十[六]分之五。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng’s Armillary Sphere says: ‘The red band spans the belly of the whole heaven, ninety-one degrees and five sixteenths from the pole.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang defines the equator at about ninety-one degrees from the celestial pole.

sentences.zh: 黃道斜帶其腹，出赤道表裡各二十四度。

translations.literal: The yellow band slants across its belly, emerging twenty-four degrees inside and outside the red band.
translations.idiomatic: The ecliptic tilts twenty-four degrees from the equator on each side.

sentences.zh: 故夏至去極六十七度而強，冬至去極百一十五度亦強也。

translations.literal: Therefore at summer solstice the distance from the pole is sixty-seven degrees and a bit strong, and at winter solstice the distance from the pole is one hundred fifteen degrees and a bit strong as well.’
translations.idiomatic: Solstitial polar distances follow from the twenty-four-degree obliquity.

sentences.zh: 然則黃道斜截赤道者，則春分、秋分之去極也。

translations.literal: Thus where the yellow band obliquely cuts the red band—that is the spring and autumn equinox distances from the pole.’
translations.idiomatic: Equinox polar distance lies where ecliptic and equator intersect.

sentences.zh: 今此春分去極九十少，秋分去極九十一少者，就夏歷景去極之法以為率也。

translations.literal: Now in this case spring equinox from the pole is ninety and a small amount weak, autumn equinox from the pole ninety-one and a small amount weak: these follow the Xia-calendar shadow method for the rate.’
translations.idiomatic: The tabulated ninety / ninety-one figures use the gnomon method as proxy.

sentences.zh: 上頭橫行第一行者，黃道進退之數也。

translations.literal: The top row, first line—the yellow path’s advance and retreat numbers.’
translations.idiomatic: That row lists ecliptic motion against the equator.

sentences.zh: 本當以銅儀日月度之，則可知也。

translations.literal: Fundamentally one ought to measure it with a bronze instrument by sun and moon positions—then one can know.’
translations.idiomatic: Ideal measurement uses a metal armillary and solar/lunar observations.

sentences.zh: 以儀一歲乃竟，而中閒又有陰雨，難卒成也。

translations.literal: With the instrument a full year is required to finish, and in between there are also cloudy and rainy days—hard to complete in haste.’
translations.idiomatic: A year of weather interrupts continuous observation.

sentences.zh: 是以作小渾，盡赤道黃道，乃各調賦三百六十五度四分之一，從冬至所在始起，令之相當值也。

translations.literal: Therefore I made a small armillary, fully inscribing the red and yellow paths, and apportioned each at three hundred sixty-five and one-quarter degrees, beginning from where winter solstice lies, and made the markings correspond to one another.’
translations.idiomatic: A desktop sphere marks both circles at 365.25° from the winter solstice point.

sentences.zh: 取北極及衡各

translations.literal: Take the north pole and the crossbar each
translations.idiomatic: Assembly step: mount pole and transverse ring.

translations.literal: (needle).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: 誠 emended to 針 ‘needle.’

sentences.zh: [針]□之為軸，取薄竹篾，穿其兩端，令兩穿中閒與渾半等，以貫之，令察之與渾相切摩也。

translations.literal: [needle] … as an axis: take a thin bamboo strip, pierce both ends, so that between the two holes the distance equals half the sphere, pass it through, and let it be seen to graze the sphere tangentially.’
translations.idiomatic: A bamboo strip on a needle axle traces the sphere’s great circle.

sentences.zh: 乃從減半起，以為[百]八十二度八分之五，盡衡減之半焉。

translations.literal: Then starting from the half reduction, take it as one hundred eighty-two degrees and five eighths, exhausting the crossbar’s half reduction.’
translations.idiomatic: Half the year’s arc is set to 182° 5/8 along the crossbar scale.

sentences.zh: 又中分其篾，拗去其半，令其半之際正直，與兩端減半相直，令篾半之際從冬至起，一度一移之，視篾之半際

translations.literal: Again bisect the strip, bend away half of it, so that at its midpoint it stands straight, aligned with the half reductions at both ends; let the strip’s midpoint start from winter solstice, moving one degree at a time, and observe at the strip’s midpoint
translations.idiomatic: The bisected strip pivots from solstice one degree per step.

translations.literal: (weak).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: 夕 emended to 少 ‘weak’ grade.

sentences.zh: 多[少]黃赤道幾也。

translations.literal: how much the yellow and red paths differ.’
translations.idiomatic: Read 多少 for the ecliptic–equator separation at each step.

sentences.zh: 其所多少，則進退之數也。

translations.literal: How much they differ is then the advance and retreat number.’
translations.idiomatic: That difference is the tabulated advance or retreat.

sentences.zh: 從

translations.literal: From
translations.idiomatic: Lemma: ‘from…’ continuing the polar-distance calculation.

translations.literal: (this).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: 此 emended to 北 ‘north.’

sentences.zh: [北]極數之，則

translations.literal: [the north] pole count them, then
translations.idiomatic: Count from the north celestial pole along the strip.

translations.literal: (distance).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: supplied reading for polar distance.

sentences.zh: [去]極之度也。

translations.literal: [from] the pole in degrees.’
translations.idiomatic: The result is angular distance from the pole.

sentences.zh: 各分赤道黃道為二十四氣，一氣相去十五度十六分之七，每一氣者，黃道進退一度焉。

translations.literal: Divide the red and yellow paths each into twenty-four qi; one qi differs by fifteen degrees and seven sixteenths; for each qi the yellow path advances or retreats one degree.’
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four solar terms, each fifteen and 7/16 degrees, one degree ecliptic motion per qi.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，黃道直時，去南北極近，其處地小，而橫行與赤道且等，故以篾度之，於赤道多也。

translations.literal: The reason is: when the yellow path is straight, it is near the south and north poles; there the earthly region is small, and the transverse motion is about equal to the red band, so measuring with the strip yields more on the equator.’
translations.idiomatic: Near solstices the ecliptic’s slant makes equatorial spacing appear larger.

sentences.zh: 設一氣令十六日者，皆常率四日差少半也。

translations.literal: Suppose one qi were sixteen days—all would follow a constant rate, short by a little less than half a day.’
translations.idiomatic: A sixteen-day qi would imply a uniform daily shortfall.

sentences.zh: 令一氣十五日不能半耳，故使中道三日之中

translations.literal: Suppose one qi is not quite fifteen and a half days—therefore in the middle course of three days
translations.idiomatic: Actual qi length is under fifteen and a half days.

translations.literal: (as if).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: 若 emended to 差 ‘shortfall.’

sentences.zh: [差]少半也。

translations.literal: [short] by a little less than half a day.’
translations.idiomatic: The three-day mid-interval is short by a fraction.

sentences.zh: 三氣一節，故四十六日而差今三度也。

translations.literal: Three qi make one node, so in forty-six days the difference is now three degrees.’
translations.idiomatic: Each three-qi node accumulates about three degrees of discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 至於差三之時，而五日同率者一，其實節之閒不能四十六日也。

translations.literal: By the time the three-degree difference arrives, there is one span of five days at the same rate; in fact between nodes it cannot be forty-six days.’
translations.idiomatic: Five-day runs equalize when the forty-six-day rule breaks down.

sentences.zh: 今殘日居其策，故五日同率也。

translations.literal: Now the leftover days occupy its reckoning, therefore the five days share the same rate.’
translations.idiomatic: Remainder days explain the five-day equal-rate segments.

sentences.zh: 其率雖同，先之皆強，後之皆弱，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Although the rate is the same, those before are all strong and those after are all weak—beyond counting.’
translations.idiomatic: Early segments read ‘strong,’ late ones ‘weak,’ in endless variation.

sentences.zh: 取至於三而復有進退者，黃道稍斜，於橫行不得度故也。

translations.literal: When one takes it to three and again there is advance or retreat, it is because the yellow path is slightly oblique and the transverse motion cannot obtain whole degrees.’
translations.idiomatic: Obliquity prevents whole-degree steps on the equator.

sentences.zh: 春分、秋分所以退者，黃道始起更斜矣，於橫行不得度故也。

translations.literal: The reason spring and autumn equinoxes retreat is that the yellow path begins to turn more oblique, and the transverse motion cannot obtain whole degrees.’
translations.idiomatic: At equinox the ecliptic angle steepens, so motion ‘retreats’ in the table.

sentences.zh: 亦每一氣一度焉，三氣一節，亦差三度也。

translations.literal: Again each qi is one degree; three qi make one node, and the difference is again three degrees.’
translations.idiomatic: The same three-degree node rule applies after equinox.

sentences.zh: 至三氣之後，稍遠而直，故橫行得度而稍進也。

translations.literal: After three qi, it is slightly farther and straighter, so the transverse motion obtains whole degrees and advances a little.’
translations.idiomatic: Past the oblique zone, motion steadies and advances.

sentences.zh: 立春、立秋橫行稍退矣，而度猶雲進者，以其所退減其所進，猶有盈餘，未盡故也。

translations.literal: At Beginning of Spring and Beginning of Autumn the transverse motion retreats slightly, yet the degree still says advance—because what it retreats is subtracted from what it advances, and there is still surplus not exhausted.’
translations.idiomatic: Net motion still advances though the oblique component retreats.

sentences.zh: 立夏、立冬橫行稍進矣，而度猶[雲]退者，以其所進，增其所退，猶有不足，未畢故也。

translations.literal: At Beginning of Summer and Beginning of Winter the transverse motion advances slightly, yet the degree still says retreat—because what it advances adds to what it retreats, and there is still shortfall not completed.’
translations.idiomatic: Net motion still retreats though the oblique component advances.

sentences.zh: 以此論之，日行非有進退，而以赤道

translations.literal: Judged this way, the sun’s daily motion does not truly advance or retreat, but measuring the yellow path with the red band
translations.idiomatic: Apparent solar motion is a projection effect of the equatorial grid.

sentences.zh: (重廣)

translations.literal: (double breadth).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: 重廣 emended to 量度 ‘measure.’

sentences.zh: [量度]黃道使之然也。

translations.literal: [measurement] of the yellow path makes it so.’
translations.idiomatic: Measuring the ecliptic against the equator produces the apparent variation.

sentences.zh: 本二十八宿相去度數，以赤道為

translations.literal: Fundamentally the twenty-eight lodges’ mutual degrees, taking the red band as
translations.idiomatic: Lodge spans are reckoned along the equator as

translations.literal: (strong).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: 強 emended to 距 ‘interval.’

sentences.zh: [距]耳，故於黃道亦[有]進退也。

translations.literal: [interval]—therefore on the yellow path there is also advance and retreat.’
translations.idiomatic: Equatorial 距 degrees project to ecliptic advance and retreat.

sentences.zh: 冬至在斗二十一度少半，最遠時也，而此歷斗二十度，俱百一十五，強矣，冬至宜與之同率焉。

translations.literal: Winter solstice lies in Dipper at twenty-one and a small half degrees—the farthest time—and in this calendar Dipper is twenty degrees, both one hundred fifteen and strong; winter solstice ought to share the same rate with it.’
translations.idiomatic: Solstice longitude and polar distance should match the tabulated Dipper entry.

sentences.zh: 夏至在井二十一度半強，最近時也，而此歷井二十三度，俱六十七度，強矣，夏至宜與之同率焉。」

translations.literal: Summer solstice lies in Well at twenty-one and a half degrees and a bit strong—the nearest time—and in this calendar Well is twenty-three degrees, both sixty-seven and strong; summer solstice ought to share the same rate with it.’
translations.idiomatic: Summer values likewise should align Well’s longitude with polar distance.

sentences.zh: 月令章句曰：「冬至之為極有三意焉：晝漏極短，去極極遠，晷景極長。

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances commentary says: ‘Winter solstice as an extremity has three meanings: the clepsydra day is shortest, the distance from the pole is farthest, and the gnomon shadow is longest.’
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu’s gloss: solstice extremes of day length, polar distance, and shadow.

sentences.zh: 極者，至而還之辭也。」

translations.literal: “Extremity” is a word for having reached the limit and turning back.’
translations.idiomatic: Ji means the turning point after maximum.

sentences.zh: 月令章句曰：「夏至之為極有三意焉：晝漏極長，去極極近，晷景極短。」

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances commentary says: ‘Summer solstice as an extremity has three meanings: the clepsydra day is longest, the distance from the pole is nearest, and the gnomon shadow is shortest.’
translations.idiomatic: Summer solstice extremes: longest day, nearest pole, shortest shadow.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕戍邊上章曰：「朔方髡鉗徒臣邕稽首再拜上書皇帝陛下：臣邕被受陛下尤異大恩，初由宰府備數典城，以叔父故□尉質時為尚書，召拜郎中，受詔詣東觀著作，遂與腢儒並拜議郎。

translations.literal: Cai Yong, shorn and collared exile on the northern frontier, bowed his head twice and submitted a memorial to His Majesty the Emperor: ‘Your servant Yong received Your Majesty’s extraordinary grace: at first through the minister’s office I was assigned to magistracies; because my uncle Zhi then served as Commandant of the Guards while he was Minister, I was summoned and appointed Gentleman of the Palace; I received an edict to go to the Eastern Pavilion to compile texts, and so together with erudite scholars I was appointed Counselor.’
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong opens his frontier memorial with his rise from local office to Eastern Pavilion compiler.

sentences.zh: 沐浴恩澤，承荅聖問，前後六年。

translations.literal: I bathed in favor and bore answers to sagely questions—for six years altogether.’
translations.idiomatic: He served six years answering imperial queries.

sentences.zh: 質奉機密，趨走目下，遂竟端右，出相好藩，還尹輦轂，旬日之中，登躡上列。

translations.literal: Zhi held confidential posts, hastening below the steps, then reaching the chief end, going out to a fine border command, returning to head the capital region; within ten days I had climbed to the upper ranks.’
translations.idiomatic: His uncle’s rapid rise from court to frontier and back mirrors Yong’s own promotion.

sentences.zh: 父子一門兼受恩寵，不能輸寫心力，以效絲發之功，一旦

translations.literal: Father and son in one household alike received favor and could not pour out heart and strength to repay even the slightest service—then in a single morning
translations.idiomatic: They could not repay the grace before disaster struck.

translations.literal: (receive).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: 披 for 被 ‘receive (the edict).’

sentences.zh: [被]章，陷沒辜戮。

translations.literal: [I received] the rescript and was plunged into guilt and execution.’
translations.idiomatic: 被章: the imperial rescript brought condemnation.

sentences.zh: 陛下天地之德，不忍刀鋸截臣首領，得就平罪，父子家屬徙充邊方，完全軀命，喘息相隨。

translations.literal: Your Majesty’s virtue is that of Heaven and earth: you could not bear to have the knife and saw cut off your servant’s head; I was allowed to settle the sentence in full; father and son and family were banished to fill the frontier posts, whole in body and life, gasping breath following breath.’
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commuted execution to family exile on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 非臣無狀所敢[復]望，非臣罪惡所當復蒙，非臣辭筆所能復陳。

translations.literal: It is not what your servant’s unworthiness would dare [again] to hope, not what your servant’s crimes ought again to receive, not what your servant’s brush can again set forth.’
translations.idiomatic: Yong disclaims any right to expect further mercy.

sentences.zh: 臣初決罪雒陽詔獄，生出牢戶，顧念元初中故尚書郎張俊，坐漏洩事，當伏重刑，已出谷門，復聽讀鞠，詔書馳救，[減罪]一等，輸作左校。

translations.literal: When your servant was first sentenced in the Luoyang imperial prison, I came forth from the cell; I thought of former Gentleman of the Palace Zhang Jun in the early Yuanchu era, who for leaking secrets faced heavy punishment, had already left the valley gate, was again summoned for trial, and by edict was rushed to rescue—[sentence reduced] one grade, labor on the left work site.’
translations.idiomatic: He recalls Zhang Jun’s reprieve from death to hard labor in Yuanchu.

sentences.zh: 俊上書謝恩，遂以轉徙。

translations.literal: Jun submitted a memorial thanking for grace, and so was transferred elsewhere.’
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun thanked the emperor and was then reassigned.

sentences.zh: [邕為]郡縣促遣，□於吏手，不得頃息，含辭抱悲，無由上達。

translations.literal: [Yong was] pressed by commandery and county officials, □ in the clerks’ hands, unable to catch a breath, holding words and embracing grief, with no way to reach the throne above.
translations.idiomatic: Urged onward by local officials and trapped in clerks’ hands, he could not rest or get his plea to the court.

sentences.zh: 既到徙所，乘塞守烽，職在候望，憂怖焦灼，無心復能操筆成草，致章闕庭。

translations.literal: Once I reached the place of banishment, I manned the passes and kept watch on the beacon fires; my duty was to stand lookout—anxious and scorched with fear, I had no heart left to take up the brush and finish a draft to present at court.
translations.idiomatic: At his frontier post he guarded beacons and could no longer draft memorials for the capital.

sentences.zh: 誠知聖朝不責臣謝，但[懷]愚心，有所不竟。

translations.literal: I truly know the sage court does not blame your servant for declining, but [I cherish] a foolish heart—there is something I could not finish.
translations.idiomatic: He knows the court does not demand thanks, yet he still grieves the work left undone.

sentences.zh: 臣自在布衣，常以為漢書十志，下盡王莽，而世祖以來，唯有紀傳，無續志者。

translations.literal: From the time I was a commoner, I always thought that the ten treatises of the Han shu run down to Wang Mang, yet from Emperor Shizu onward there are only annals and biographies, with no one to continue the treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Since his commoner days he had noted the Later Han lacked treatises to match Ban Gu’s ten monographs.

sentences.zh: 臣所師事故太傅胡廣，知臣頗識其門戶，略以所有舊事[與臣]，雖未備悉，粗見首尾，積累思惟，二十餘年。

translations.literal: My late teacher, the former Grand Tutor Hu Guang, knew that your servant was fairly familiar with their outlines; with the old materials he had [for me]—though not exhaustive—I could see beginning and end; pondering and accumulating more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang had shared materials with him for over twenty years, enough to see the shape of a continuation.

sentences.zh: 不在其位，非外吏庶人所得擅述。

translations.literal: Not holding the proper office, it is not for an outer clerk or commoner to presume to compose.
translations.idiomatic: Without rank, a private scholar may not author such state papers.

sentences.zh: 天誘其衷，得備著作郎，建言十志皆當撰錄，遂與議郎張華等分受之，

translations.literal: Heaven moved his inmost heart: I was appointed Compiler, and I proposed that the ten treatises should all be set down; so together with Counselor Zhang Hua and others we divided the task among ourselves,
translations.idiomatic: Once appointed at the Eastern Pavilion, he proposed the ten treatises and split the labor with Zhang Hua and colleagues.

sentences.zh: (所使元順)

translations.literal: (The phrase 「所使元順」).
translations.idiomatic: Apparatus gloss for the four-character phrase later emended per Cai Yong’s anthology.

sentences.zh: [其]難者皆以付臣。

translations.literal: [As for] the difficult parts, all were entrusted to your servant.
translations.idiomatic: The hardest sections fell to him alone.

sentences.zh: 先治律歷，以籌筭為本，天文為驗，請太

translations.literal: First working on statutes and calendrics, taking rod reckoning as foundation and astronomy as verification, I ask that the Grand
translations.idiomatic: He began with law and the calendar, grounding the work in computation and checking it against the sky.

translations.literal: (Preceptor).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: the title element 師 (emended to 史 ‘Astrologer’).

sentences.zh: [史]舊注，考校連年，往往頗有差舛，當有增損，乃可施行，為無窮法。

translations.literal: [Astrologer] old commentary—examined and collated over successive years—often has discrepancies; there must be additions and subtractions before it can be put in force as a lasting standard.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Astrologer’s old commentary needed years of collation before it could serve as a durable norm.

sentences.zh: 道至深微，不敢獨議。

translations.literal: The way is exceedingly subtle; I dare not deliberate alone.
translations.idiomatic: The technical material was too subtle to settle privately.

sentences.zh: 郎中劉洪，密於用筭，故臣表上洪，與共參思圖牒。

translations.literal: Gentleman Liu Hong was skilled in the use of the counting rods; therefore your servant memorialized recommending Hong to join me in pondering the charts and registers.
translations.idiomatic: He brought in Liu Hong, expert at rod calculus, to work through the tables with him.

sentences.zh: 尋繹適有頭角，會臣被罪，

translations.literal: Tracing it out, there happened to be a beginning, when your servant suffered punishment,
translations.idiomatic: The project had barely taken shape when he was condemned.

translations.literal: (Then).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: manuscript 遂 (emended to 逐).

sentences.zh: [逐]放邊野。

translations.literal: [I was] driven out to the frontier wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Banishment to the border cut the work short.

sentences.zh: 臣竊自痛，一為不善，使史籍所闕，

translations.literal: Your servant privately grieves: in one stroke of misdoing I have caused the historical records to lack what they need,
translations.idiomatic: He blames his crime for leaving the dynastic record incomplete.

translations.literal: (Therefore).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: 故 (emended to 胡 for Hu Guang).

sentences.zh: [胡]廣所校，二十年之思，中道廢絕，不得究竟。

translations.literal: [Hu] Guang’s collation—twenty years of thought—was cut off halfway and could not be brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang’s twenty-year editorial effort was broken off mid-course.

sentences.zh: 慺慺之情，猶以結心，不能違望。

translations.literal: With anxious care the feeling still ties my heart; I cannot turn away from what I hoped.
translations.idiomatic: He still cannot abandon the hope of finishing the treatises.

sentences.zh: 臣初欲須刑竟，乃因縣道，具以狀聞。

translations.literal: At first I wished to wait until punishment was finished, then by county relay present the full account.
translations.idiomatic: He had planned to report through frontier channels once his sentence ended.

sentences.zh: 今年七月九日，匈奴始攻郡鹽池縣，其時鮮卑連犯雲中、五原，一月之中，烽火不絕。

translations.literal: This year on the ninth day of the seventh month the Xiongnu first attacked Yanchi County in the commandery; at that time the Xianbei repeatedly raided Yunzhong and Wuyuan—within a single month the beacon fires never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Xiongnu and Xianbei raids kept the frontier beacons burning without pause.

sentences.zh: 不

translations.literal: Lemma: negative particle.
translations.idiomatic: Negation at line start.

sentences.zh: (言四)

translations.literal: (言四).
translations.idiomatic: Spurious characters 言四 in the received text, struck per Lu Wenchao.

sentences.zh: [意西]夷相與合謀，所圖廣遠，恐遂為變，不知所濟。

translations.literal: [The western] barbarians plot together—their designs are broad and far-reaching; I fear they will soon turn to rebellion—I do not know where it will lead.
translations.idiomatic: He fears the western tribes are conspiring on a large scale and may soon rise—outcome unknown.

sentences.zh: 郡縣鹹懼，不守朝旦。

translations.literal: Commanderies and counties alike are terrified and may not hold out until morning.
translations.idiomatic: Local defenses might not last the night.

sentences.zh: 臣所在孤危，懸命鋒鏑，湮滅土灰，呼吸無期。

translations.literal: Where your servant stands is isolated and perilous; my life hangs on blades and arrowheads—I may be ground to dust in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: His own life on the frontier hangs by a thread amid the fighting.

sentences.zh: 誠恐所懷隨軀腐朽，抱恨黃泉，遂不設施，謹先顛踣。

translations.literal: I truly fear what I carry in my heart will rot away with my body, leaving regret in the Yellow Springs, and so I set nothing down—therefore I first stumble and fall forward with this plea.
translations.idiomatic: Lest his plans die with him, he risks this memorial though it may mean his fall.

sentences.zh: 科條諸志，臣欲

translations.literal: As for the various treatises by topic, your servant wishes
translations.idiomatic: He outlines the treatise plan: first,

translations.literal: (to compile).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: 制 read as editorial ‘compile and fix.’

sentences.zh: 刪定者一，所當接續者四，前志所無，臣欲著者

translations.literal: to delete and fix one, to continue four where connection is needed, and for what the former treatises lack, your servant wishes to compose
translations.idiomatic: One treatise to redact, four to continue, and new sections for gaps in the old Han shu.

translations.literal: (three).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: manuscript three (emended to five).

sentences.zh: [五]，及經典腢書所宜捃摭，本奏詔書所當依據，分別首目，並書章左。

translations.literal: [five], together with what the classics and erudite literature ought to gather, and the edicts that should serve as authority—dividing into headings and items, all listed at the left of the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Five new monographs plus sources from classics and edicts, with headings listed on the left.

sentences.zh: 臣初被考，妻子迸竄，亡失文書，無所案請。

translations.literal: When your servant was first interrogated, wife and children fled in all directions, and documents were lost—there was nothing to consult.
translations.idiomatic: His arrest scattered his family and destroyed his papers.

sentences.zh: 加以惶怖愁恐，思念荒散，十分不得識一，所識者又恐謬誤。

translations.literal: Added to that were panic, fear, and grief—thoughts scattered in confusion—I retain not one part in ten of what I knew, and of what I retain I still fear error.
translations.idiomatic: Terror has erased nine-tenths of what he remembered; the rest may still be wrong.

sentences.zh: 觸冒死罪，披

translations.literal: Braving capital offense, I spread open—
translations.idiomatic: He risks death to open his breast and begin the plea that follows.

translations.literal: (pour out).
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: 散 emended to 瀝 ‘pour out’ (瀝愚情).

sentences.zh: [瀝]愚情，願下東觀，推求諸奏，參以璽書，以補綴遺闕，昭明國體。

translations.literal: [and pour out] my foolish feelings: I beg that it be sent down to the Eastern Pavilion, that you may pursue the various memorials, compare them with the imperial seals’ documents, and thereby patch what is missing and make the body of the state clear.
translations.idiomatic: He asks the court to lodge the plea at the Eastern Pavilion and cross-check memorials and sealed edicts to repair the record.

sentences.zh: 章聞之後，雖肝腦流離，白骨剖破，無所復恨。

translations.literal: After the memorial is heard, though my liver and brains be scattered and my white bones split, I shall have no further regret.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor has seen it, he accepts any execution without regret.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下省察。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty examine it.
translations.idiomatic: He begs the emperor’s judgment.

sentences.zh: 謹因臨戎長霍圉封上。

translations.literal: Respectfully submitted by frontier captain Huoyu in sealed envelope.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial is sealed and sent through the frontier captain Huoyu.

sentences.zh: 臣頓首死罪稽首再拜以聞。

translations.literal: Your servant bows his head, guilty of death, bows his head again twice, and submits this for your hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Closing formula: obeisance and submission.

sentences.zh: 」其所論志，志家未以成書，如有異同，今隨事注之於本志也。

translations.literal: ’ As for the treatises he discussed, the compilers had not yet completed the book; where there are differences, notes are now appended to this treatise according to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial closing: Cai Yong’s treatise plan was never finished as a book; divergent details are annotated here in the present monograph.
